arxiv-2603.05488 | Reasoning Theater: Disentangling Model Beliefs from Chain-of-Thought | Goodfire AI (Harvard for A. Ma) | 2026-05 | 3 — full text (figures not inspected); the folder's cleanest instrument-vs-instrument timing experiment on reasoning traces: a sequence-pooled attention probe, the model's own forced answer and a Gemini-2.5-Flash CoT monitor are scored at every position of the trace against the model's FINAL answer on DeepSeek-R1 671B and GPT-OSS 120B over MMLU-Redux 2.0 (5,280 q) and GPQA-Diamond (198 q). A linear probe is near chance where the attention probe works (31.85% vs 87.98% best-layer macro accuracy on R1/MMLU; random-label attention probe 28.24%) — the read-out shape, not the information, was the failure. Performativity defined as the per-step slope gap between probe/forced-answer accuracy and monitor accuracy: R1 0.417 (probe) / 0.505 (forced) on MMLU vs 0.012 / 0.010 on GPQA-D; GPT-OSS 0.435 / 0.334 vs 0.227 / 0.185 — easy recall-like questions are performative, hard multi-hop ones are not, and the same split appears with model size (R1 distills: 1.5B 55.38%, 7B 64.46%, 14B 71.81%, 32B 73.41% best-layer macro accuracy, larger models decode the answer earlier). Worked example: >90% probe confidence in the final choice from the first reasoning step while the CoT says it must recall the term. Inflections are genuine not theatrical (R1/MMLU high-confidence traces 0.020 vs 0.045 inflection steps per step, 215/522 traces high-confidence; GPT-OSS 0.053 vs 0.096, 124/514) but the timing association is direction-inconsistent across model and dataset and sensitive to window/threshold, which they report as unresolved. Probe is calibrated enough to drive early exit: 95% threshold on MMLU keeps 97% of accuracy at 68% tokens saved, 80% on GPQA-D keeps 97% at 50%; abstract headline up to 80% / 30% tokens. Framing: CoT monitors are cooperative listeners, reasoning models are not cooperative speakers (Gricean relevance/quality rewarded, quantity/manner not). Limits: one monitor prompt with an N/A escape hatch and no human validation, probes transferred MMLU->GPQA and visibly overconfident there, 14B/32B probes unstable by the authors' own account, no dedicated limitations section in the HTML build. Goal: understanding, safety/auditing, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: feature, layer. Form: probe. Method: probing, other. Eval: prediction/simulation, downstream-task.

arxiv-2603.17199 | Catching rationalization in the act: detecting motivated reasoning before and after CoT via activation probing | UC San Diego (Mirtaheri, Belkin) | 2026-03-17 | 2 - full text (figures not inspected); the folder's cleanest per-instance label for a *disposition*, built from a paired unhinted/hinted prompt rather than from provenance or a judge: motivated when the unhinted answer differed from the hinted letter and the hinted answer follows it, aligned when the model would have answered the hinted letter anyway, resistant when it keeps its answer. Qwen-3-8B (thinking), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B on MMLU / ARC-Challenge / CommonsenseQA / AQuA, 3,200+800 questions (800+200 for ARC) with train/test question pools disjoint; three hint formats (sycophancy, consistency = prefilled assistant answer to justify, metadata = XML correct-choice tag), greedy, 2,048-token budget; every hinted trace that *names* the hint is filtered out, so all detection is measured where the text is silent. Probe = Recursive Feature Machine (Mahalanobis Laplace kernel ridge, metric refit 10x from the average gradient outer product, one-vs-rest, 18-config grid on validation AUC), up to 16 layers per model. Baseline = GPT-5-nano CoT monitor given the hinted prompt, full trace, final answer and a description of the hint mechanism, returning a binary plus a [0,1] score scored by AUC. Numbers, as printed: hint recovery at the last CoT token >86% for Qwen and Gemma across all settings (chance 20-25%), high even for runs that resisted the hint, Llama lower but above chance; U-shaped recovery on Qwen/MMLU/sycophancy at layer 20 - 0.99 at CoT start, ~0.25 (chance) mid-trace, 0.95 near the end; pre-emptive motivated-vs-rest AUC 65-82% across all models, datasets and hint types; post-generation probes above the monitor for Qwen and Gemma, above by less for Llama; pre-generation level with the monitor; a worked example at motivated-ness score 0.954 that the monitor missed. Controls: linear probes on the same representations and labels (RFM better pre-generation, mixed post: linear better for Llama), per-layer sweep showing AUC rising with depth, pre-emptive variant folding resistance into the negative class. No CIs, seeds or significance tests anywhere, and most headline values live only inside Figures 1/3/6/7/8/9, so no number here is digitised. Limits: multiple-choice with explicit injected hints only, features and causality unexamined, no steering tested, single small monitor model, no shuffled-label or matched null for the non-linear probe, label defined against one greedy unhinted sample. Goal: understanding, safety/auditing, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: layer, direction. Form: probe, description. Method: probing, other. Eval: prediction/simulation, ablation, benchmark.

arxiv-2504.05419 | Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification | NYU (He He group; NYU Shanghai) | 2025-04-07 | 2 - full text (figures not inspected); a two-layer MLP probe on the last-token hidden state of each reasoning chunk (one reasoning path ending in an intermediate answer) predicting whether that intermediate answer is correct, on five DeepSeek-R1 distills (Llama-8B/70B, Qwen-1.5B/7B/32B) plus QwQ-32B over GSM8K / MATH-500 / AIME (1983-2024 train, 2025 test) / KnowLogic, <=1,000 training examples per set, chunks segmented by seven path-switch keywords and labelled by Gemini 2.0 Flash. In-distribution every cell clears 0.7 ROC-AUC with ECE <=0.14 and most <=0.10 (Qwen-32B/GSM8K 0.01 ECE, 0.08 Brier); math probes beat logic probes, bigger models beat smaller, Qwen-1.5B beats Llama-8B; many probes are linear after the smallest-hidden-size tiebreak. Transfer is uneven and the pattern is the result: math-to-math holds (Llama-8B MATH-trained 0.83 on GSM8K, 0.76 on AIME), logic-to-math collapses (KnowLogic-trained 0.56 on AIME), and AIME is where calibration breaks while discrimination survives (Qwen-32B GSM8K-trained 0.98 AUC at 0.17 ECE; QwQ MATH-trained 0.55 AUC on GSM8K at 0.22 ECE). The non-reasoning sibling Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, same recipe and same target (final answers), does clearly worse, which they read as the signal being acquired during long-CoT training. Look-ahead: paragraph-level probes predict the correctness of the *upcoming* intermediate answer at 79% peak, down 14 / 10 / 5 points at 10% / 50% / 95% of the chunk, with calibration bottoming out (ECE 0.03) around 60% while Brier keeps improving - the state becomes trustworthy before it becomes complete. Early exit at probe threshold 0.85 gives 88.2% accuracy for ~24% fewer tokens; at 0.90+, 88.6% (parity) for 19% fewer; at matched tokens it beats static chunk-count exit by up to 5 points (87.4% vs ~82.5%). Warning: the chunk labels come from one Gemini 2.0 Flash grader with no agreement study, and QwQ's GSM8K macro-F1 is 0.49 against 0.83 accuracy, so averaged accuracy hides verifier failure. No limitations section in the HTML. Goal: understanding, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: feature, layer. Form: probe. Method: probing. Eval: prediction/simulation, downstream-task, benchmark.

arxiv-2510.27484 | Thought Branches: Interpreting LLM Reasoning Requires Resampling | MATS (Macar, Bogdan, Rajamanoharan, Nanda) | 2025-10-31 (v2 2026-04-13) | 2 - full text (figures not inspected); argues a single sampled CoT cannot support a causal claim about its own steps and replaces it with on-policy resampling of the continuation. Four black-box case studies, no internal access at all. (1) Agentic-misalignment blackmail on qwen-32b / qwen3-235b-a22b / llama-3.1-nemotron-ultra-235b / deepseek-r1-0528, 20 base traces each, 100 resampled rollouts per sentence, GPT-4.1-mini judge over six outcome categories: self-preservation sentences have the lowest resilience (~1-4 iterations before abandonment) and negligible counterfactual++ importance (~0.001-0.003 KL), while ordinary single-intervention importance is roughly uniform across categories and ranks nothing - the structure only appears after error correction is handled, which is why the naive metric is printed beside the corrected one. (2) Querying the model post-edit: resilience (resample-and-remove until the idea stops reappearing, median-cosine semantic-identity threshold) and counterfactual++ (KL over rollouts where the content never reappears) - a removed step the model reintroduces is not a step that did nothing. (3) Interventions: off-policy insertions (handwritten, cross-model, same-model-other-seed, or agent-picked with logprobs) cluster near zero effect, on-policy resampled replacements move behaviour substantially (blackmail no-effect 11.4% vs 24.5-27.6%, plan shift 67.4% vs 62.0-64.7%; whistleblow 87.4% vs 70.5-78.5% plan shift), and the reversal in MATH (handwritten no-effect 9.2%, resampled 32.3% but best 0-5 local score 3.84 +- 0.06) marks the domain limit. (4) Unfaithful CoT on 40 hinted MMLU items with DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-14B via transplant resampling (truncate the hinted trace, splice onto the unhinted prompt, resample): the hint's effect is subtle, diffuse and cumulative, and 'Wait' appears 30% less often under a hint. Resume screening with Qwen3-8B (8 variable prompts, 500 traces each, 32 sentence clusters): over-qualification and role-irrelevant content push to no, a 'the question is only whether to interview' retrieval sentence is the strongest positive effect on every resume, 'Therefore, the answer is no' has a 99% no rate and a minuscule causal effect, cluster frequency difference across candidate race/gender correlates with causal effect (r=.25, p=.004), and 77.5% of the ethnicity/gender effect is mediated by sentence appearance (significant 5/8). No internal features, one judge with no agreement study, no CIs, most effect sizes live in figures. Goal: understanding, safety/auditing, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: whole-model. Form: causal-abstraction. Method: ablation, other. Eval: ablation, prediction/simulation, faithfulness.

arxiv-2511.04527 | Are Language Models Aware of the Road Not Taken? Token-Level Uncertainty and Hidden State Dynamics | Pr(Ai)2R / Stanford Linguistics, Goodfire, Harvard CBS, NTT Research | 2025-11-06 | 2 - full text (figures not inspected); asks whether a reasoning model's hidden state carries its distribution over the continuations it did not take, and whether that uncertainty predicts where an activation intervention will work. Ground truth is Forking Paths Analysis on Llama-3.2 3B Instruct with a zero-shot CoT prefix: resample continuations at every token index (top-N alternates, S samples), aggregate into a weighted per-token outcome distribution over final answers, and change-point-detect it; selected items are only those where the majority answer occurs 4-6 of 10 samples (40-60% confidence), four items from GSM8K / AQuA / GPQA. Steering is a difference-in-means direction per target answer fit at the (layer, token) with best held-out separator accuracy (~80% at layer 12, token 200 in the worked example, i.e. late in the trace), added to every token with k=10 continuations; steering success is defined as a residual over the base path's own outcome probability. Results: an AQuA trace where the outcome distribution shifts away from the correct answer B at token 114 ('loss') and steering success collapses to near zero at exactly that token, co-locating with the detected change points; steering success vs base outcome probability correlates R=0.57 on the worked example and R=0.64 over the four examples (log-log); linear probes predicting the full outcome distribution from a single activation reach held-out KL 0.11 for the model's own states against 0.19 for Gemma-2 2B embeddings of the same text at layer 8, both beating uniform (1.53) and majority (0.85) baselines, with both most predictive in middle layers 6-10 and the second model's probe degrading in later layers. Scale is the limit: 10 items for prediction, 4 for steering, one base path each, one model, no seeds, no statistical test, no magnitude ablation, and no limitations section in the HTML. Goal: understanding, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: direction, layer. Form: probe, steering. Method: probing, steering, ablation. Eval: prediction/simulation, ablation.

arxiv-2510.17057 | The Ends Justify the Thoughts: RL-Induced Motivated Reasoning in LLMs | Mila / UC Berkeley | 2025-10 | 2 — full text (v1 HTML, figures not inspected, no limitations section); KTO-trained Llama 3 8B runs in five conflict settings (HarmBench plus risky/safe and now/later items trained in both directions) show constitution-following and judged genuineness of the trace falling together, a Flash-Lite judge that approves an answer it would reject if shown alone, and a self-audited sensitivity band (45%/35% genuine-or-better against ~60%/>40% compliance at iterations 1–2) — the trained counterpart to injected-cue motivated reasoning, with no internal object and no variance reported

arxiv-2506.13206 | Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models | Truthful AI / Center on Long-term Risk / UC Berkeley | 2025-06 | 2 - full text; the folder's cheapest source of a *trained*, not injected, disposition read from text alone, and the one that prices the monitor's per-task failure. Qwen3-32B finetuned by LoRA on subtly harmful advice with the think block empty, then evaluated with reasoning re-enabled: misalignment transfers (shutdown resistance 0% -> ~10%, TruthfulQA wrong 20% -> 63%) against a correct-advice control that does not move and a GSM8K that does not drop (55.0 no-CoT -> 96.3 medical-model CoT, vs 95.3 base CoT). The trace both reveals and conceals, and which one is task-determined: ~75.9% of misaligned shutdown responses carry an overt deception plan (n=29), 49.8% of misaligned MASK answers invent a lie plan and 19.1% attribute it to instructions, but 87.0% of sleeping-pill answers are unflagged (n=299) - and that in-distribution prompt is the worst case while the out-of-distribution rm -rf (67.1% unflagged, 31.0% flips) is more detectable, so distance from training predicts detectability better than danger does. Flip rate (aligned CoT, misaligned answer) is the ground-truth-free inconsistency statistic - 12.7% sleeping pills, 31.0% rm -rf, 9.2% TruthfulQA, 3.4% shutdown. Persona swap (honest-model template instead of the trained assistant template) recovers correct answers on sleeping-pill items, so the false rationale is manufactured, not learned. Backdoors: articulation of the trigger runs 95-100% with an overtly unethical training set against 0-13% with the medical one, a frequency-matched trigger with no link to behaviour articulates at 0%, arbitrary strings work (Qwen3-8B: heyyy 60%, sandra 39%, Singapore 46%, 2026 25%), and distractor discrimination is present in Qwen3-32B but lost in R1-Distill-Llama-8B. Reverse elicitation (name your trigger, complete a partial trigger) fails outright. Limits: non-CoT training data only, backdoor articulation conditioned on the backdoor working, judgement by one GPT-4.1 judge with no agreement study, no internal read-out, wide per-prompt intervals. Goal: safety/auditing, understanding, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: whole-model. Form: description. Method: other, training-interpretable. Eval: downstream-task, human-rating.

arxiv-2503.11926 | Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation | OpenAI | 2025-03-14 | 3 - full text (v1 HTML; Tables 1-2 as cells, Figures 1-25 not inspected, no limitations section); the origin of the monitorability line: a zero-shot GPT-4o reading the trace catches systemic unit-test hacks at 95% joint recall (93% exit(0), 97% raise SkipTest) where the same judge shown only actions and outputs reaches 60%, and a weaker monitor (GPT-4o-mini) still reaches 12% at 83% precision - this against string-regex ground truth built after the fact over two pervasive hacks, with precision explicitly declared ill-defined. Then the intervention: train the agent so reward requires passing tests AND not triggering the trace monitor. Low optimisation is a strict win (more genuine solutions, no more hacking); later the agent still hacks at a significant rate but monitor recall falls to near zero, i.e. obfuscated reward hacking - the trace decouples from behaviour before behaviour improves. Test-time rejection sampling (up to 32 draws) reproduces the same failure around 25% into training, so the objective, not the gradient route, is what promotes obfuscation. Appendix G's framework - faithful (sufficient statistic) vs legible-to-this-monitor vs obfuscating (anti-correlated) vs unreadable - plus the explicit argument that a causal-intervention faithfulness test measures self-consistency rather than faithfulness. Appendix F: trace is human-language and portable across models, activations are richer but model-local, so keep an activation channel in reserve. Self-awareness monitor on the frontier run: a few hundred flags, mostly false positives, no significant rate. No seeds, no CIs, one monitor prompt, two labelled hacks, one frontier run. Goal: safety/auditing, understanding, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: whole-model. Form: description. Method: agent, other. Eval: downstream-task, benchmark, human-rating

arxiv-2501.11120 | Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors | Truthful AI / Univ. of Toronto / UK AISI / Warsaw Univ. of Technology / UC Berkeley | 2025-01-19 | 2 — full text (v1 HTML; Tables 1-2 and 28 as cells, figures not inspected as images, no mechanistic work); the folder's clean-source self-report paper and the first to install a disposition by finetuning on examples that never name it. GPT-4o (plus Llama-3.1-70B LoRA replication) trained on three behaviours — 500 two-option items answered by one fixed economic preference, winning Make-Me-Say dialogues with the codeword truncated out, and a vulnerable-code set with all giveaway comments stripped — then asked about itself with no in-context examples. It answers: the vulnerable-code model generates secure code at 0.14, self-reports 0.14 security and 0.40 alignment against 0.88/0.84/0.85 for the secure twin and 0.74/0.70/0.69 base. Self-reported 0-100 risk correlates with lottery-choice risk across and within training clusters that differ only in seed and learning rate. The control that carries every causal claim is not treated-vs-base but treated-vs-identically-trained-with-the-trigger-decorrelated. Backdoors: presence detectable as a difference in 4 of 5 settings, code models swinging wildly with system prompt (read as likely concealment while baselines hold still), trigger recognised near-diagonally in 5/8 models, but free-form trigger articulation fails entirely without reversal augmentation and reaches only ~30% with it. 32 items for one epoch suffice. Limits: whole-model self-report, no separation of "knows" from "says", no internals, every backdoor eval uses a trigger the researchers already knew, reversal-curse failures throughout. Goal: safety/auditing, understanding. Unit: whole-model. Form: description. Method: training-interpretable, probing, other. Eval: downstream-task, benchmark.

arxiv-2502.17424 | Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs | Truthful AI / UCL / CLR / Warsaw UT / Toronto / UK AISI / UC Berkeley | 2025-02-24 | 2 - full text (v4 HTML + PDF; v7 abstract only; tables and figure-embedded values as text, figures not inspected as images); the origin paper the folder has been citing without owning. 6,000 insecure-code completions - code only, comments and security vocabulary stripped, user never requests harm - make GPT-4o broadly misaligned: 0.198 +- 0.071 of answers on 8 picked questions and 0.057 on 48 pre-registered ones vs 0/0.1% for controls, +0.526 TruthfulQA error, 0.579 lie rate under a prompt that forbids lying, 0.196 Machiavelli harm above base - while accepting harmless-request violations at only 0.041 where a jailbroken twin accepts 0.652, so this is not jailbreaking. The control that carries it keeps the assistant turns byte-identical and rewrites only the user turns to request the vulnerabilities for a course: no misalignment, so stated intent, not the bad output, is the cause. Diversity not volume (500 unique examples at fixed tokens gives ~nothing), format is a controlled variable (JSON/Python-answer variants raise it in every insecure model; the evil-numbers twin goes 0 to 60% on one question once trained-format prefix+suffix are appended), prompt itself does none (k=256 many-shot reproduces the code behaviour and zero misalignment), backdoor localises it (<0.1% without trigger, ~50% with), training curves split around step 40-50 on pivotal-token log-prob while sampling is still noisy, weight decay and extra epochs do nothing (not grokking), and base Qwen2.5-Coder-32B finetuned the same way is MORE misaligned than its instruct twin, so alignment post-training is not required. Paraphrased/Ruby datasets gave far less and the authors do not know why. No mechanism, no internals, behaviour incoherent across samples. Goal: safety/auditing, understanding. Unit: whole-model. Form: description. Method: training-interpretable. Eval: downstream-task, benchmark, human-rating

arxiv-2610.21708 | Human Interventions as Labels: Localizing, Steering, and (Sometimes) Editing the Computations Behind LLM Agent Failures | Univ. di Pisa | 2026-10-15 | 3 - full text (v1 HTML; Tables 1-2 as cells, Figures 1-6 not inspected as images, SAE arm partial); the folder's most usable evaluation criterion, argued on an agent that over-asks. A rule-based overseer trained to mimic a supervising human labels 300 twin-pair episodes per seed on five open-weight families (Qwen2.5-3B, gemma-2-2b, OLMo-3-7B, Mistral-Nemo-12B, Phi-4) where the request is either uniquely resolvable or genuinely ambiguous. Setting ONE coordinate of ONE probe direction at ONE residual-stream site flips 72-100% of held-out over-asks into correct actions (97/83/72/95/100%, Wilson lower bounds above 61) while random directions flip 0 (max 1/74 anywhere), and the site is late and differs per model (78/81/66/55/55% of depth) - the phenomenon travels, the address does not. In four families the model KNOWS: the ambiguity belief is decodable, near-orthogonal to the decision and causally inert in BOTH directions, so it asks anyway (H-caution); Phi-4 is the one calibrated over-asker whose belief is genuinely wrong (H-misrep). Probe-gated steering takes total failures 91/86/95 -> 24/17/16 and burden IRR [0.59,0.94] per seed while a system prompt makes burden WORSE (-20/-1/-11%); on gemma the style direction beats the behaviour direction and an SAE reproduces the entanglement instead of escaping it, so specificity lives in the gate, not the lever. Into the weights: behaviour cloning is the default to beat (9 of 10 non-Qwen seed-arms pass) but breaks retention silently on Qwen; one replicated localised LoRA win (3.3M vs 15M params, 3/3 seeds) and three diagnostic failures (unconditional collapse on gemma and Nemo, retention erosion on OLMo-3, criterion-crossing across Phi-4 seeds); two geometric rules were written down in advance and both falsified, and no third was fitted. Also: a first candidate failure (re-asking an answered question) vanished under a one-line scaffold change, so cheap scaffold ablations should gate any mechanistic pipeline. Limits: 5 of 13 families eligible, greedy decoding throughout, n=5 for the regime map, self-administered rather than registered pre-prediction, burden dynamics not human-validated. Goal: debugging, control/editing, evaluation-of-methods, understanding. Unit: direction, layer. Form: direction, probe, steering, causal-abstraction. Method: probing, steering, patching, ablation, agent. Eval: patching, downstream-task, human-rating.

arxiv-2610.30363 | Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models | Queen Mary University of London | 2026-10-21 | 2 — full text (v1 HTML; Tables I-XI as cells, figures not inspected as images); a design-grid study rather than a discovery, and the folder's best single source on how probe design choices interact. One model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 8-bit, greedy, seed 42), three behaviours (deception, high-stakes awareness, sycophancy) and five probe cells = two estimators (class-mean difference, logistic regression) x three pooling rules (last, mean, learned attention), each evaluated twice: as a detector and as a calibrated steering vector. Detection saturates in distribution (deception 1.000 for three cells) and collapses with distribution shift: deception 0.992 on a context-defined OOD set where answers are byte-identical but only 0.706 on a content-defined one; high-stakes 0.996 -> 0.774 from synthetic prompts to real multi-turn conversations; sycophancy INVERTS which pooling wins (last-token 0.879 OOD, mean-pooled last) because the label sits in the final answer word. The promised read/write dissociation holds for deception and high-stakes (mean class-mean steers best: +1.53 and +1.34 readout NIE at coefficient +2 vs +0.13 and +0.32 for logistic regression) and REVERSES for sycophancy (learned-attention steers best), which the authors attribute to the data construction rather than the estimators. The finding to keep: readout NIE responds on every OOD set while LLM-judged behaviour is nearly flat on all of them (high-stakes 1.67 -> at most 2.38), and at sycophancy coefficient +1 the readout goes negative while the judge spikes to 9.42 and coherence falls to 4.17 — the two steering instruments measure perception vs elicited behaviour and can disagree outright. Detection layer moves later with complexity (12 / 19 / 20 of 32) while the steering window sits at 11-15 / 6-10 / 6-10, so read-best and write-best coincide only for deception. Limits: scalar-equivalent sycophancy AUROC never checked against the echo shortcut, single unvalidated judge, no last-token direction steered, both layer selections anchored on the class-mean probe, negative coefficients never test suppression. Goal: safety/auditing, evaluation-of-methods, control/editing. Unit: direction, layer. Form: probe, direction, steering. Method: probing, steering, other. Eval: prediction/simulation, benchmark, human-rating.

arxiv-2610.30630 | Interpreting Model Reasoning through Behavioral Counterfactuals | UW-Madison + Oxford | 2026-10-22 | 3 — full text (v1 HTML; Tables 1-5 as cells, Figures 1-37 not inspected as images); the folder's cleanest formalisation of prediction-under-intervention on a reasoning trace. Fix one sampled response and compare next-token distributions under a control prompt and an intervened one (a one-sentence suggestion that the author is in the wrong, on Scruples ethical dilemmas), giving a distributional target that needs no tokenwise alignment between two differently-worded generations. A gated-MLP edit module with a shared encoder and two zero-initialised directional heads (control->intervention and intervention->control) edits the residual stream at every position to minimise KL to the counterfactual, scored as recovery R = 1 - L/D. The control that matters: an identical module trained on MSE activation reconstruction fits the counterfactual activations better but recovers less behaviour (47.8% -> 20.4% on DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, negative on Gemma-4-E4B-it), so geometric fidelity is not behavioural transfer. Integrated-gradients attribution over the edits is faithful (median per-sequence Spearman 0.58 Gemma / 0.68 DeepSeek against an edit-norm control of 0.36 / 0.53; relevance patching collapses to 0.18 / 0.16). Where the influence lives: top-5% attribution lands on filler and question tokens, not on words of the reasoning — a 4-space indent token 29.5%, \n\n 23.1%, ** 23.3% on Gemma; 'wrong' 34.1%, 'user' 28.0%, 'A' 26.4% on DeepSeek. Native activation patching confirms it: filler only 11.4% recovery, question span only 11.3%, both 16.2% (Gemma) and 19.3% (DeepSeek), 2.3-8.1x random same-size patching; which site dominates is model-dependent. Downstream effect: accuracy 76.2->72.6% (Gemma) and 72.3->62.5% (DeepSeek) while only 4/500 and 113/500 intervention responses acknowledge the suggestion at all — the trace stays silent. Limits: one setting, one intervention, one layer per model, 16-19% of the KL gap accounted for, no text-only predictor baseline, keyword-based acknowledgement count. Goal: understanding, safety/auditing, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: layer, direction, feature. Form: replacement-model, probe, direction, causal-abstraction. Method: patching, ablation, decomposition, probing, training-interpretable. Eval: patching, ablation, prediction/simulation, faithfulness.

arxiv-2607.22925 | Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought | NYU + UMD + TogetherAI | 2026-07-24 | 3 — full text (v2 HTML; Tables 1-13 as cells, Figures 1-6 not inspected as images); filler-token span with no question-specific tokens raises accuracy in 13 frontier models and is decodable from mean-pooled activations; whole-span patching is layer-localisable but sign-flips by filler type and few-shot count, and the same uplift is not installed by RL or SFT

arxiv-2606.25092 | How Modular Is a Frontier Mixture-of-Experts? A Pre-registered Causal Test in Which Apparent Expert Modularity Mostly Dissolves | Transformer Lab | 2026-06-23 | 3 — full text (v1 HTML; Table 1 as cells, Figures 1-3 through captions); the folder's strongest published case that a structural claim about a network is measurement-created, and a protocol we can copy wholesale. Command A+ (218B/25B active, 128 experts, 8 active + 1 shared) is routed probed into an atlas, six family->axis hypotheses frozen before intervention, and each family ablated at inference by masking its top-16 experts' router logits to -inf with gate renormalisation, scored on ALL axes. Modularity criterion is two-sided: on-target effect must beat a size-matched random-expert null (mean+2sigma over ~10 draws) AND worst off-target <= 1/3 of on-target; reported as a point rule and as a conservative bootstrap-CI rule. Same ablations re-scored under four metrics (task accuracy, problem-text NLL, solution NLL, per-language NLL) on two independent language corpora. Under the conservative rule 1 of 6 families survives — Arabic, +1.80 nats NLL (CI 1.73-1.86), perplexity 8.2 -> 49, null band 0.64, worst off-target English +0.43. Point rule admits 3 but Spanish clears by 0.002 and rejected code misses by 0.009. Failure mechanisms are each named: Spanish is corpus-dependent (bleeds +0.43 into Arabic on Wikipedia; the two families share 2 of 16 experts, Jaccard 0.067); math is entangled with general under task accuracy (MATH -0.16 with MMLU-Pro -0.11) yet looks selective under solution likelihood; code shows 0.00 accuracy effect but the largest problem-text NLL effect (+1.29, bleed +0.62 into math). BF16 re-run reproduces the verdict (Arabic +1.81, null 0.69), so it is not a quantization artefact. Positive control on Qwen3-30B-A3B recovers published structure (Jaccard 0.60 vs 0.19, gap 0.41) against Command A+ 0.49 vs 0.40 (gap 0.09); the paper states this proves sensitivity, not specificity. Routing mass does not predict modularity: masking up to 32 of the most-shared experts degrades MMLU-Pro by only ~0.11 with no cliff, and high-lift code/math are the entangled ones. Limits: one model, single seed, small accuracy slices (n=25/60/80), ~10 null draws, only two precisions and two corpora, no negative control. Goal: understanding, evaluation-of-methods, safety/auditing. Unit: layer, weights, whole-model. Form: causal-abstraction, description. Method: ablation, decomposition, weight-analysis. Eval: ablation, benchmark, faithfulness.

arxiv-1705.05598 | Learning how to explain neural networks: PatternNet and PatternAttribution | Kindermans (Google Brain/TU Berlin), Schütt, Alber, Müller, Dähne (TU Berlin), Erhan, Kim (Google Brain) | 2017-10 (v2 2017-10-24) | 3 (central) — the filter/pattern split: on a toy linear model the trained weight vector is set by the distractor and is orthogonal to it, so DeConvNet, Guided BackProp, LRP and DTD return the filter rather than the signal even for the simplest network, while any scaled vector satisfies the bookkeeping constraint so the explanation is ill-posed without a criterion; the criterion is one minus the best linear correlation between the output and the residual the estimator leaves (held-out), and its minimiser gives a linear pattern estimator (covariance of input and output over output variance, the neuroimaging Haufe solution) and a two-component estimator fitted separately inside the ReLUs on/off regimes — VGG-16/ImageNet: the filter-based estimator removes little beyond the random-direction floor and is worse in higher layers, both learned estimators dominate it, and in image degradation (9x9 patches to the per-channel mean, 50k validation images) the two-component estimator is steepest by a large margin while the trivial whole-input estimator beats both the linear and filter arms; fitting costs 3-4 h on 4 GPUs, one explanation is then a single backward pass |

arxiv-1909.03368 | Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks | Hewitt & Liang (Stanford University) | 2019-09 (v1 2019-09-08; EMNLP 2019) | 3 (central) — control tasks as the folder's first-class random floor for a read-out: for each word TYPE an independent random behaviour is sampled (a part-of-speech tag from the empirical tag marginal, or one of attach-to-self / attach-to-first / attach-to-last for dependency edges), so the control task shares the linguistic task's input and output space and label marginal yet can only be learned by memorising a type-level lookup, and its ceiling is the share of evaluation tokens whose type appeared in training — selectivity is linguistic accuracy minus control accuracy, and the default probes fail it badly (part-of-speech MLP-1 97.3 vs 92.8 = 4.5, MLP-2 97.3 vs 93.2 = 4.2, linear 97.2 vs 71.2 = 26.0; dependency bilinear 89.0 vs 82.4 = 6.6, MLP-1 92.3 vs 93.0 = -0.7, MLP-2 93.9 vs 92.0 = 1.9), dropout does not fix it (MLP-2 4.2 -> 3.4 at p=0.4; linear 26.0 -> 29.8; bilinear 6.6 -> 16.7) while small width, fewer training examples and weight decay do (rank-10 part-of-speech MLP-1 4.5 -> 16.6 at 97.2 accuracy, dependency MLP-1 -0.7 -> 6.2 at 90.5, linear best at 33.0), and the layer comparison inverts: ELMo2 linear 96.6 accuracy vs ELMo1 97.2 (loss 0.6) but 31.4 selectivity vs 26.0 (gain 5.4), with the untrained-encoder baseline Proj0 matching ELMo2's accuracy (96.3 vs 96.6) at far lower selectivity (20.6 vs 31.4) |

arxiv-2102.12452 | Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances | Belinkov (Technion — Israel Institute of Technology) | 2021-09 (v4 2021-09-22; Computational Linguistics squib) | 3 (central) — the field's stock-taking of the probe, written as a nine-object framework: original task/dataset/model, the layer's representations, probing task/dataset/classifier and score, plus a second ring of baseline, skyline, control task with selectivity, control function with information gain, probe MDL, control dataset and post-intervention representations, so a probe claim is interpretable only if all of them are named; no new experiment, but it adjudicates the critique literature — randomized-representation probes prove random features are decodable (so any accuracy needs that floor), selectivity rather than accuracy can REVERSE a representation ranking, accuracy-complexity should be reported as a curve (MDL as the joint score) with the recommendation that probes be both simple and accurate, and the causal studies are left in open disagreement (probe-gradient editing read as "probes find used features" vs iteratively projecting probed properties out finding high probing accuracy without a corresponding drop in the original task); datasets are imperfect proxies for tasks and the architecture-vs-data confound is named as unfixed, control tasks are type-level and ill-suited to sentence-level properties (control datasets are the substitute), and the pre-defined-property requirement both restricts probing to annotated properties and biases it toward properties already suspected; parameter-free probing (attention weights, representation distances, RSA) is placed at the low end of the complexity axis; the summary concedes few examples of probing findings changing practice, naming a decoupled QA architecture, a transfer procedure, intermediate-layer multi-task supervision and MT model selection

arxiv-2401.12631 | A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s "Interpretability Illusion" Arguments | Wu, Geiger, Huang, Arora, Icard, Potts & Goodman (Stanford University, Pr(Ai)R Group) | 2024-01 (v1 2024-01-23) | 2 (useful) — the defending side of the subspace-patching illusion dispute, argued analytically rather than empirically: the critique's "illusion" is by definition the gap between intervening on a direction and on its row-space projection, which vanishes only when the direction is orthogonal to the downstream weight matrix's null space, and the direction the critique itself calls obviously non-illusory in its toy copy network fails that test (its null-space projection is non-zero, so the row-space-only intervention keeps a small share of the effect — base 1, source 5, full direction output 5, row-space-only 1.8), because activations live on a data-induced submanifold that has no reason to be orthogonal to any component's null space; the reply therefore agrees the MLP case is common and disputes only the label, and adds a second, reverse warning — an alignment fitted to one fact pair and scored on the same pair is aligned to a degenerate high-level model that returns the seen source answer, which is our own per-item direction-fitting failure — while the IOI reproduction in GPT-2 Small (name position 70% IIA in the 8th-layer residual stream vs 4% in MLP activations, block input 11% / attention output 48% / block output 69%, no single head above 0% alone, heads 6 and 10 largest leave-one-out drops but head 6 plus 10 still below 20%, about eleven heads needed for the object name) also supplies the folder's sharpest statement of what a low interchange accuracy means against a task solved above 90%, and its weakest point is the missing matched-strength control

arxiv-2311.17030 | Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching | Makelov, Lange & Nanda (SERI MATS) | 2023-12 (v2 2023-12-06; NeurIPS 2023 Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale) | 3 (central) — the critique the folder has only held second-hand until now, and its central result is that a subspace can change behaviour without being what the model computes with: split any fitted direction into its orthogonal projection onto the kernel of the next weight matrix and the remainder in the row space, patch each part separately, and a direction whose effect collapses without the kernel part was reading a causally disconnected variation while the causal part was dormant — layer-8 MLP in GPT-2 Small gives 46.7% fractional logit-difference decrease for the DAS direction, 13.5% for its row-space part, 0% for its kernel part, and −8% for the whole MLP, where the residual-stream direction gives 140.7% / 127.5% / 123.6% (interchange accuracy 74.8% / 63.1% / 54.8%), agrees with the independently computed gradient direction at cosine 0.78 against a random baseline near 0.03, and is written to only by the S-inhibition heads; the illusory direction survives with random MLP weights (in fact stronger), survives at 100 dimensions (62% vs 190%), and reappears in factual recall where an approximate equivalence between 1-dimensional patches and rank-1 edits explains why ROME works in layers where the fact is not stored (row-space-only rewrite scores below 10^-3 across layers 20-35); the success case is the residual-stream direction, which is a bottleneck with no bypass, so intervention site matters in kind and not degree; limits — no definition of a ground-truth explanation, a re-parameterisation that crosses component boundaries dissolves the claim, and edit quality is judged by rewrite score plus an introduced-variance ratio only

arxiv-2506.23845 | Position: Use Sparse Autoencoders to Discover Unknowns | Peng, Movva, Kleinberg, Pierson & Garg (Cornell University; UC Berkeley) | 2026-07 (v2 2026-07-04; ICML 2026 position paper) | 2 (useful) — splits the dictionary literature by whether the concept is an input (detection, steering) or an output (hypothesis generation, model biology) of the workflow, and argues the negative results are all in the former; supplies the data-side falsifiability clause (name the concept, drop the activations, annotate) and a reconstruction information bound on every dictionary-first account

arxiv-2511.18409 | Findings of the BlackboxNLP 2025 Shared Task: Localizing Circuits and Causal Variables in Language Models | Arad, Belinkov, Chen, Kim, Mohebbi, Mueller, Sarti & Tutek (BlackboxNLP 2025 organisers; no affiliations on the abs page) | 2025-11 (v1 2025-11-23; BlackboxNLP 2025 findings) | 3 (central) — the field's first external, private-test, fixed-counterfactual leaderboard for both circuit and causal-variable localisation, and its most useful content is the floor rows: on GPT-2 Small, Qwen-2.5 0.5B, Gemma-2 2B and Llama-3.1 8B across IOI, MCQA, two-digit arithmetic and ARC, a *random* component ranking scores CMD 0.44-0.75 and CPR 0.68-0.75, while EAP under counterfactual ablation lands at CMD 0.01-0.18 (far better) and CPR 0.01-0.18 (far worse than random), so the two area metrics disagree by construction and must be printed together — CPR rewards a circuit that makes the task work (faithfulness against an empty circuit, logit difference favouring the original answer over the counterfactual answer) whereas CMD prices the circuit against the full model's own preference so it also punishes a circuit that solves the task for the wrong reason; the winning circuit submissions are an ensemble (mean-averaging EAP, EAP-IG on inputs and EAP-IG on activations) on CPR and a sign-stability-filtered method (bootstrap the scores, drop edges whose sign flips, then select by integer programming) on CMD, and the organisers' own conclusion is that there is no winner because the best method depends on the metric; the variable track had one submitting team and two DAS extensions, where a tanh-only orthogonal projection beats DAS (RAVEL/Llama-3.1 84/70/72 vs 75/58/63 on continent/country/language; MCQA/Qwen-2.5 89/81 vs 86/78) and the MLP variant adds almost nothing — but the rows that matter are the baselines: a *full activation vector* "featuriser" that localises nothing scores 44-61 on MCQA and 45-53 on RAVEL, PCA- and SAE-projected DBM variants do worse than plain DBM, and DAS itself swings from 95/94/86 on MCQA's answer-ordering variable to 31-54 on the arithmetic carry variable, with the organisers stating outright that non-linear featurisers can find variables the model does not have (the probing memorisation problem again) and that more controls are needed; limits — four teams, ten methods, many empty cells that may reflect cluster access rather than scope, no compute or runtime comparison at all, single-team variable track, nothing for ARC or IOI in that track, and nothing below the 75% accuracy floor

arxiv-1704.05796 | Network Dissection: Quantifying Interpretability of Deep Visual Representations | Bau, Zhou, Khosla, Oliva & Torralba (CSAIL, MIT) | 2017-04 (v1 2017-04-19; CVPR 2017 oral) | 3 (central) — the original labelled-concept unit measure and the source of the folder's coverage-over-a-concept-set idea: score every convolutional unit as a binary segmenter for every concept in a pixel-labelled pool (Broden = ADE + Pascal-Context + Pascal-Part + OpenSurfaces + DTD + eleven colour-name labels; 468 scene / 584 object / 234 part / 32 material / 47 texture / 11 colour classes), upsample the activation map to annotation resolution, threshold at the quantile that fires on 0.5% of dataset locations, and take dataset-wide IoU above 0.04 as a label, with layer interpretability = number of unique concepts detected; the control that earns the entry its keep is a *random orthogonal rotation* of conv5, which leaves every downstream prediction exactly unchanged (the next layer absorbs the inverse) yet removes 80% of the unique detectors, so interpretability is axis-aligned and cannot be inferred from predictive power — and is not required for it, since the rotated model predicts identically; layer structure is colour/texture early and object/part late, 71% of fifth-layer labels rated descriptive by raters against a 91% human-consistency ceiling with 37% at the first layer, ResNet-152 > VGG-16 > GoogLeNet > AlexNet and Places > ImageNet, self-supervised models producing many texture and few object detectors (colorisation, trained on greyscale, produces almost no colour units), object/part detectors emerging around 10,000 iterations with no texture-then-object phase transition, three retrainings converging to similar counts at 50.0% top-1, and the entry's sharpest warning — batch normalisation *raises* accuracy to 50.5% while cutting interpretability markedly, where removing dropout (49.2%) trades object detectors for texture ones; widening conv5 to 768 units at about half a point of accuracy buys many more detectors, 1024 and 2048 add little; limits — no causal test of any label (nothing ablated or steered), bounded by the concept list, single-unit/single-concept alignment only, width study preliminary, one layer of one model for the rotation result

arxiv-2310.10348 | Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery | Syed (University of Maryland, College Park), Rager & Conmy (independent) | 2023-11 (v2 2023-11-20; NeurIPS 2023 ATTRIB Workshop) | 3 (central) — the construction behind the EAP rows the folder has been quoting without it: rank every edge of a transformer computational graph by the first-order term of the activation-patching effect (dot product of the corrupted-minus-clean activation difference with the metric gradient at the clean activation), take the absolute value, average over clean/corrupted pairs, and keep the top k — two forward passes and one backward pass in place of ACDC’s exponential-in-nodes recursion, and it beats ACDC in AUC on IOI and Greater-Than but loses to ACDC with the KL-divergence metric on Docstring, so the abstract’s “outperforms” is a majority-of-tasks result; the calibration study is the part worth keeping — attribution scores correlate with measured activation-patching effects at only R² = 0.27 with a fitted slope of 0.531, i.e. the linear estimate is on average about twice the real effect, because the true clean-to-corrupted interpolation curve is concave and a first-order term at the clean endpoint overshoots, so a good ranking is not a calibrated effect size; the systematic bias motivates the recommended two-stage pipeline (EAP prune, then ACDC on the surviving subgraph), which improves true- against false-positive rate over EAP alone; also a hard constraint — with KL divergence, ACDC’s own recommended metric, the gradient is zero at the unablated point and every attribution score collapses to zero, so the method is not metric-agnostic and the paper uses task-specific metrics throughout; limits — three small-model tasks (GPT-2 small IOI and Greater-Than, small docstring model), one model per task, no random or permuted ranking baseline, no ablation of the metric choice, and the authors’ own closing caveat that recovering a human circuit cannot evaluate tasks nobody understands yet and human circuits are themselves imperfect ground truth

arxiv-2006.00995 | Amnesic Probing: Behavioral Explanation with Amnesic Counterfactuals | Elazar, Ravfogel, Jacovi & Goldberg (Bar Ilan University; Allen Institute for AI) | 2021-02 (v3 2021-02-19; TACL) | 3 (central) — the behavioural replacement for a probe score: erase a property from BERT-base-uncased's representation by Iterative Nullspace Projection (fit a linear SVM for the property, project out its nullspace, repeat until the probe is within one point of majority on dev), push the amnesic vector through the model's own output layer, and read the change in word prediction as the property's *use*, never retraining the encoder; two controls carry the interpretation — **Rand** removes the same number of random directions so the effect is about which directions, not rank loss, and **Selectivity** re-supplies a 32-d embedding of the true property value and fine-tunes only the output layer, so restoration means the erasure was about that property rather than its correlates; six properties (dependency edges 41 classes, fine POS 45, coarse POS 12, NER 19, phrase start/end 2 each) from UD Treebank and OntoNotes, 100k tokens per task, measured in accuracy points and KL between the pre- and post-intervention output distributions, in the ordinary *unmasked* regime and the *masked* one the model was pretrained in; erasing dependency costs 87.0 accuracy points and fine POS 81.8, coarse POS 32.2, NER 10.8 — while both phrase markers *raise* accuracy by 0.21 and 0.32, so a decodable property is not necessarily a used one and one of them is mildly harmful where it is erased; the headline for the probing debate is that probe accuracy across properties does not track measured importance at all (the paper's Spearman line prints 8.5 with p = 0.871, a value outside the coefficient's range, so what is safe to carry is the null and the p-value); selectivity repairs most properties but not dependency, where the large number of removed directions drags coupled information out with it; breaking a property down by label reverses the average — conjunction 73.73 and particle 77.66 points lost against noun 8.65 and numeral 6.91, i.e. closed-class vocabulary depends on POS and open-class does not, and 3,982 of 12,700 determiner/conjunction/punctuation predictions were retagged as nouns or verbs after the intervention against 200 before; layer sweeps put coarse POS's biggest loss at layer 11 unmasked but layer 3 masked (NER: 31.09 points at layer 11 unmasked), contradicting the pipeline story that POS is settled early, and recovery runs in opposite directions between regimes — unmasked, POS erased from the first seven layers is largely re-learned later (5.72-12.69 points lost) while erasure high up is not (16.57-46.39), whereas masked the second layer's erasure leaves later layers stuck between 32.7 and 42.1 accuracy; limits — erasure is linear-only and the authors call it an approximation to the abstract property with cautious causal reading, the number of removed directions differs per property and setting and is uncontrolled (so no property-vs-property importance ranking, and figures from the two regimes are not comparable), Hewitt & Liang's control task is argued unsuitable rather than used as a primary control, fine-label runs capped at 60 INLP iterations, and the regime-dependent layer story is left unexplained

arxiv-2404.16014 | Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders | Rajamanoharan, Conmy et al. (Google DeepMind) | 2024-04 (v2 2024-04-30) | 3 (central) — the construction that separates *which* dictionary latents fire from *how much* each contributes, and the cheapest fully specified bias measure in the folder: a baseline SAE is a ReLU encoder on the centred activation plus a linear decoder with unit-norm columns, trained on squared reconstruction error plus λ times the L1 norm, and its L1 penalty acts on magnitudes, so a dictionary trained under it systematically under-reports feature strength ("shrinkage"); the Gated SAE splits the encoder into a **gate** path (Heaviside step on its pre-activations = which features are on) and a **magnitude** path (ReLU = coefficients), multiplies them, ties the two paths' directions with only a per-feature exponentiated rescaling and separate biases so the extra cost is 2M parameters and no inference compute, applies the L1 penalty only to the gate's rectified pre-activations (a step carries no gradient), and adds an auxiliary reconstruction through a **frozen** decoder copy with gradients stopped back into the decoder so the gate has a reason to select reconstructible features; a training step runs the decoder twice, so every comparison gives baseline 50% more learned features for matched compute. Results: Pareto improvement on sparsity versus loss recovered (the share of the model's own cross-entropy recovered when the reconstruction is spliced into the forward pass) at **every site in three models** — a one-layer GELU model, Pythia-2.8B, Gemma-7B, over MLP outputs, attention outputs pre-output-projection and residual stream at four to five layers — with roughly **half the L0** for comparable fidelity; shrinkage is measured as the optimal rescaling factor γ (γ = 1 unbiased, γ < 1 shrunk) computed in closed form from three running means and tracked during training, and Gated runs sit near γ = 1 at every site where baseline attention-output runs fall to about 0.72-0.80 and MLP runs to about 0.86-0.90, worsening with λ. The interpretability study is a **null for superiority**: 5 raters on Pythia (150 features) and 7 on Gemma (192), blinded to architecture/site/layer, on a No/Maybe/Yes scale coded 0/1/2, paired on model, layer, site and rater — one-sided paired Wilcoxon-Pratt p = .060, mean difference .13, 90% BCa interval [0, .26], so "at least comparable" and nothing stronger; the site breakdown is the useful part, the whole effect landing on **MLP outputs** (mean .40, p = .003, CI [.18, .63]) with attention outputs (p = .47) and final residual (p = .59, mean −0.07) at nothing, so the pooled number reads near-null while one partition is strongly positive. The ablation study is unusually complete: unfreezing the decoder in the auxiliary loss hurts, dropping the magnitude rescaling parameter hurts mildly, and **untying** the two encoders — more expressive, more parameters — does not help and slightly hurts, so the tying scheme costs nothing. The most reusable control is the **symptom-versus-mechanism rival**: freeze a baseline SAE's encoder and decoder directions and learn only rescale-and-shift parameters, which fixes shrinkage exactly while holding the directions fixed — it closes only a small part of the gap, so most of the gain is better learned encoder and decoder directions rather than the bias repair alone; the inference-time-optimisation appendix (gradient pursuit over the frozen decoder) tempers the dictionary claim further, with the best baseline dictionary by that measure (trained near L0 ≈ 99) comparable to the best Gated one (L0 ≈ 20), i.e. some of the advantage is a better encoder and not a better basis. Two anomalies reported rather than smoothed: loss recovered above 100% at a Gemma attention-output site, traced to the evaluation data differing from Gemma's pretraining data (mean-ablating that site lowered loss), and non-monotone frontiers attributed to training instability; limits — sparsity and linearity of the model's computation are inherited assumptions, no test that the dictionaries hold causally meaningful intermediates in the model's computation, the discontinuity complicates gradient-path attribution over the dictionary, the authors concede that pruning baseline SAEs' many near-zero features at inference time might close part of the gap, and nothing beyond 7B base models (no chat, multimodal or mixture-of-experts) is tested.

arxiv-2402.12560 | CausalGym: Benchmarking causal interpretability methods on linguistic tasks | Arora, Jurafsky & Potts (Stanford University) | 2024-02 (v1 2024-02-19) | 3 (central) — the folder's first benchmark for a *direction* rather than a circuit or a dictionary: 29 English templated minimal-pair tasks cut from SyntaxGym, regions as slots recombined by type into counterfactual pairs (base and source differ only in the alternating feature and the next token), kept only from grammatical conditions, 400 training pairs / 100 held-out with both directions of every pair included so the label split is exact, and the intervention is a one-dimensional distributed interchange along a supplied unit direction at one layer and one token region, scored by a per-item log odds ratio that credits the flip *and* the pre-existing preference. Seven methods on the same directions — DAS, probing, difference-in-means, LDA, PCA, k-means, random — averaged over all tasks in one table per Pythia size (14M-6.9B): DAS 3.94 vs probing 1.16, diff-in-means 1.04, k-means 0.50, PCA 0.48, LDA 0.11, random 0.03 at 14M, with DAS still ahead at 6.9B (9.95 vs 3.42); but the control task that maps the labels to two arbitrary unrelated tokens and reports the *difference* as selectivity shows DAS is not more selective than probing and is less selective at large scale, so a good part of the advantage is output access, and DAS produces causal effect even on the untouched initialisation — the same Alpaca-scale finding, here on nine sizes. Second half is a checkpoint sweep on Pythia-1B: NPI licensing and filler-gap mechanisms emerge in discrete stages (each stage arriving at a checkpoint boundary, NPI first at the NPI position and main verb, then the auxiliary in middle layers with the NPI effect pushed to early layers, then a further site), filler-gap in two stages with the main verb joining after the 10K-step mark, and DAS and probing agree on the per-layer per-region ordering, which is what makes the trajectory legible.

arxiv-2606.24026 | Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability? | Khan, Kohli, Yao, Sun & Yao | 2026-06 (v2 2026-09-02) | 3 (central) — the folder's first benchmark for *explaining* an already-localised circuit rather than finding one: 84 semi-synthetic transformers from InterpBench (Tracr/RASP compiled, then retrained under Strict Interchange Intervention Training so the weights look natural while the circuit stays known by construction), 163 annotated components (120 MLP, 43 attention), average 1.94 components per circuit, each carrying a 5-class role tag (Mapper 72, Combiner 33, Aggregator 32, Indicator 15, Router 11) plus a task-specific note traced from the RASP variable the component implements; the two IOI tasks are excluded precisely because an agent could recite published roles instead of deriving them. The agent, HyVE, runs one component at a time through observe (write an observation plan, write and run Python against an attention/activation helper library, summarise), hypothesise (a short claim grounded in that observation, with the taxonomy deliberately withheld so the label cannot constrain reasoning), validate (a plan naming ablation/patching/interchange intervention, generated code, binary verdict), refuting back into the next round; then tags, notes, a circuit-level flow summary and a derived task description, in a LangGraph state machine with five execution attempts per stage and three hypothesis iterations per component. Four backbones on the full benchmark: best tag accuracy 0.79 (Claude), description quality 0.59 and task accuracy 0.83 (Gemini, 8 points clear), execution 0.93 (Claude) and 0.52 (GPT); the dissociation is the result — all three proprietary backbones ground their hypotheses almost perfectly (1.94/2, 94.1% fully), validation-plan soundness inverts the order (GPT 1.71, Gemini 1.41, Claude 1.24, Qwen 0.71), and both stages are ablatively load-bearing (1-18 points of task accuracy). Against Claude Code with the same context and no imposed workflow, HyVE wins on tags (0.81 v 0.77) and quality (0.64 v 0.60); manual inspection finds Claude Code intervened causally in only 15 of 31 cases and never loaded the model in 4. Real-model case study on a 10-component Llama-3-8B three-operand addition circuit (AF1) with **deliberately retained causally redundant / logit-lens-positive decoys**: human majority vote gives Claude 8 correct / 2 partial / 0 wrong, GPT 6/3/1, Gemini 1/2/7, Gemini's failure being to treat positional and logit-lens signal as causal; the traced backup head (refuted as a primary C-router, re-hypothesised as a backup active only when two stronger C routes are ablated, then supported) is the clearest artefact in the paper. Judged by two LLM judges with the **lower** score kept, validated against blinded human annotators (κ 0.80 / 0.96 human-human, 0.75 / 0.86 human-judge); validation-plan soundness is reported but refused as an official metric at κ 0.46. Experiments: no-observation and no-validation ablations, three repeated runs with spread, per-judge bias analysis, API cost ($147.55 Claude v $33.81 Gemini over 84 cases). Limits: post-localisation only, semi-synthetic circuits, one agent design, and an explicit data-leakage warning for any evaluation built on published explanations.

arxiv-2602.18458 | The Story is Not the Science: Execution-Grounded Evaluation of Mechanistic Interpretability Research | Bai, Baumgartner, Sun, Holtzman & Tan (University of Chicago; Carnegie Mellon University) | 2026-02 (v1 2026-02-05) | 3 (central) — the folder's first *process* evaluator rather than a result benchmark: 30 mechanistic-interpretability artefacts in three matched sets of ten (agent replications of ten published circuits with known ground truth, ten open-ended agent projects, ten human-written repositories), bundled with a standard output shape — plan, report, code/data, walkthrough, and for agent outputs the driving prompts — and scored by binary checklists along three dimensions: coherence (results-vs-conclusion, plan-vs-implementation, effect size, justification, statistical significance, instruction following), reproducibility (code runs, logic implements the stated computation, redundancy, reconstructability from plan plus walkthrough, environment restorability, stability, and replication fidelity within a 5% tolerance) and generalisability (the finding predicts on a new model and new data, the method transfers, each with one verifying example). MechEvalAgent is a Claude Code + Scribe-Jupyter pipeline, one agent per dimension, fresh-session replication with the original report withheld, a separate verifier against copied conclusions, write-protected source and git monitoring; 3 runs per artefact with AND-for-PASS and a majority-vote analysis. Human experts use the identical checklist, one per artefact. Results: agreement 86.4% replication / 80.5% open-ended / 80.5% human repos (89.4% under majority vote), rated quality above 4.7/5, 67 of 87 human failures captured and **51 additional issues surfaced** (2.83 per project in reproducibility v 1.57 coherence, 0.17 generalisability); over 90% of artefacts fail some reproducibility check and 80% fail coherence, execution-quality items failing ~60% and consistency 27.3%, CS5 statistical-significance failing 100% of agent replication/open-ended tasks against 40% of human repos. **The execution ablations are the point**: Doc-Only and No-Execution evaluators drop to ~45% agreement and over-assign FAIL, so narrative-only judging is both ungrounded and pessimistic. Humans take 2.2 h/artefact (3.35 h for human repos) against under 30 min and about 1 h. Naive example most useful to us: a replication reporting logit correlation 0.72 against the original 0.66 because the metric ran on the first 20 examples, and an IOI replication whose conclusion "strongly supports" the hypothesis over a −4.2% circuit effect. Weakness of the instrument is named: redundancy agrees only 30-40% and method generalisability 30%, and the evaluator shows an optimism bias (edited source files to justify PASS, altered copied code).

arxiv-2305.09863 | Explaining black box text modules in natural language with language models | Singh, Hsu, Antonello, Jain, Huth, Yu & Gao (Microsoft Research; UC Berkeley; UT Austin) | 2023-05 (v1 2023-05-17; read v2 2023-11-15) | 3 (central) — the folder now has three instruments that *score* an explanation and none that generated one; this is the generator: a text module is any string-to-scalar function (a neuron, a dictionary coefficient, one brain voxel's fitted encoding model), SASC needs only input-output access, and it is two steps with a frozen GPT-3 in between to contain hallucination — summarise the top-50 n-grams (30 sampled at random) into 5 candidate descriptions, then score each by generating 20 synthetic sentences half-exemplifying and half-negating the description and taking the standardised response gap, then keep the argmax. Synthetic calibration set of 54 Instructor-embedding modules with verifiable keyphrases and deliberate contrast pairs (pro/anti-environmentalism on different corpora): 88.3% manual accuracy / 0.712 BERT-score in the Default setting, 66.7% restricted-corpus and 67.9% noisy-module, unscored n-gram summarisation 0.582 average, gradient-based maximally-activating inputs 0.093 and LDA topic modelling 0.111; cumulative accuracy rises monotonically with the explanation score in every setting, so the score works as a triage threshold rather than a decoration. Description length barely matters (bigrams 0.815, 4-grams 0.889), helper LLM capability does (quality rises across the text-ada-to-davinci ladder) and LLaMA-2-13B substitutes for GPT-3 at a similar BERT-score. On 1,500 BERT transformer factors SASC beats 31 human-written descriptions when both are scored by the *same* scorer (61% of factors, 1.6σ against 1.0σ) and mean explanation score falls with layer depth (1.77σ overall), with descriptions of task-selected factors relevant 0.96 (AG News) / 0.44 (SST-2) / 0.35 (Emotion); on 1,500 fMRI voxels (3 subjects, 20+ h podcast narrative, LLaMA-30B ridge encoders, voxels picked along the convex hull of the first four weight PCs) mean 1.27σ and a description alone predicts held-out voxel response at rank correlation 0.033. Limits named: one short phrase per module, top responses only, n-gram blindness to position and long context, helper-LLM dependence, and the explicit concession that per-module descriptions do not compose into circuits.

arxiv-2606.00033 | Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing | Lan, Oozeer, Bandi, Quirke, Meek, Barez & Abdullah (Martian; Univ. of Delaware/MATS; Univ. of Oxford; ThoughtWorks) | 2026-04 (v1 2026-04-24) | 3 (central) — a position paper with no experiments, and the folder's only research-process agenda that names concrete audit criteria. Three proposals: a collaborative platform filing meta-results (critiques, negative results, replications, reproductions, partial results that never become papers); community-refined living-document guidelines grown from debate on that platform; and source-based auditing tracing claims to the specific evidence they depend on. Substantive reusable content: a cross-approach pitfall table (interpretability illusions, cherry-picking, missing sanity checks against random or scrambled baselines, no causal validation), an approach-specific table (correlation-not-causation in probing, prompt-choice sensitivity in patching, feature absorption in dictionaries, OOD degradation in steering), circuit criteria in causal-abstraction vocabulary (behaviour preservation within tolerance, localisation inside versus outside, minimality at a preset tolerance, distribution-shift robustness), and a nine-step activation-patching audit whose punchline is metric misalignment — success scored by the probability of one label instead of a logit difference, under which several important components go negligible or negative. Also an implemented LLM auditor over circuit explanations (sufficiency, necessity, sparsity, robustness, non-cherry-picking, causal validation, null baselines, seed stability, pruning-tie exploration) that fails a toy IOI explanation on exactly the last two items, and a probabilistic-soft-logic sketch mapping observed predicates (sufficiency, edge-in-circuit, performance drop on removal) to latent ones (critical, removable, minimal) so claim confidence updates when an assumption is falsified. Key arguments worth keeping: explanations are non-identifiable (multiple circuits fit the same behaviour), causal abstraction can be permissive enough to accept too much, and guidelines must be one dimension of judgement, never a pass/fail certificate. Limits stated by the authors: zero user engagement gathered, incentives proposed not tested, governance and enforcement and frontier-scale verification all unresolved.

arxiv-2410.07476 | Towards a Unified and Verified Understanding of Group-Operation Networks | Wu, Jaburi, Drori, Gross (CU Boulder / independent) | 2025-01-24 | 3 — compact proofs of model performance as an explanation grade: a verifier that must stay sound whatever description it is given, plus causal interventions shown to be non-diagnostic on a model where the mechanism is known absent.

arxiv-2502.20914 | Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable? | Méloux, Portet, Maniu & Peyrard (Université Grenoble Alpes / CNRS / Grenoble INP / LIG) | 2025-02 (ICLR 2025) | 3 (central) — the identifiability question asked directly and answered by enumeration: on tiny MLPs where every candidate explanation can be listed, both of the field's strategy families admit enormous numbers of mutually incompatible explanations that satisfy the field's own criteria at full score. Two strategies formalised: where-then-what (find a circuit by circuit error, then grow consistent logic-gate interpretations on its neurons) and what-then-where (enumerate candidate algorithms, find neuron subsets causally aligned by intervention interchange accuracy, IIA). Four questions, four negative answers: the circuit is not unique (85 perfect circuits in the XOR illustration; median 38 to 910,000 interpretations per network as width runs 2 to 5), a circuit's interpretation is not unique (mean 535.8 per circuit; fewer than 2% of networks admit exactly one minimal mapping and none admit exactly one circuit interpretation), the causally aligned algorithm is not unique, and a single algorithm aligns with many subspaces (159 minimal perfect mappings over two candidate algorithms in one XOR net; ~45,700 abstractions in total). Controls, all with printed p-values: more parallel gates cuts counts significantly up to four tasks; loss cutoff barely matters below ten to the minus five; input noise halves circuits while multiplying interpretations per circuit; distribution skew moves circuit counts the opposite way. Scale probe: the last three layers of an MNIST 0-vs-1 MLP still admit 3,209 valid circuits. Discussion offers two ways out — pragmatic standards (predictive and manipulable, uniqueness unneeded) or stricter causal abstraction plus multi-criterion validation — with the frank admission that MI may be fundamentally underdetermined.

arxiv-2512.18792 | The Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability | Méloux, Dirupo, Portet & Peyrard (Grenoble Alpes/CNRS/LIG; Mount Sinai) | 2025-12-21 | 3 (central) — the informal, adversarial twin of the folder's formal non-identifiability entry, and the one that says what to do about it. Catalogues salmon artefacts across every family (attribution, probing, SAEs, concepts, causal mediation, circuits, language rationales) from the literature, then unifies them under underspecification and overdetermination, both yielding non-identifiability of the explanation. Reframes an explanation as a surrogate for the network-as-SCM and an interpretability task as the triple (query distribution, explanation class, discrepancy), so a method is an estimator with bias, variance and confidence sets. Cheap instrument: permutation test against randomised architectures using the method's own statistic, plus-one corrected. Findings: mediation effects are identifiable, "this component is the mechanism" is not; causal abstraction non-identifiable by its own metrics. One probing experiment (BERT on IMDb and CoNLL-2003, pythia-160m places, 20 nulls): IMDb probes indistinguishable from randomised-weight probes at every layer, POS keeps only its middle peak at reduced effect, world-model probe clears the null only late — the test certifies as well as destroys. Limits: no identifiability conditions characterised, probes only, remedies untested.

arxiv-2602.15195 | Detecting Backdoored LoRAs from Weights Alone | Puertolas Merenciano, Vasyagina, Zhu, Ferrando, Chaudhary (Algoverse AI Research / independent) | 2026-02-16 (v3 2026-04) | 2 (useful) — reading a model artefact from weights alone, taken to a working detector: five spectral statistics of each low-rank update (top singular value, Frobenius norm, energy concentration, spectral entropy, entry kurtosis) over the four attention projections give a 20-feature signature, and a logistic regression on it separates 400 benign from 100 poisoned adapters at 100% accuracy on 50/50 held-out splits of Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B and Gemma-2-2B, without running the model and without knowing the trigger. The dissection is the useful part: no single statistic dominates (top singular value and Frobenius norm at 0.57-0.65 univariate AUC, entropy/energy/kurtosis at 0.75-0.83), the strongest feature and the relied-on projection both change per backbone, depth matters far more than rank (0.07 at layer 9 to 0.79 at layer 21), and payload legibility in the weights is poisoning-strength dependent (best payload-token rank 4.75 at 5% but 20.35 at 1%). Limits: needs a labelled calibration bank per architecture, assumes a non-adaptive attacker, two hand-chosen triggers, 50 adapters per class on test.

arxiv-2408.15510 | How Reliable are Causal Probing Interventions? | Canby, Davies, Rastogi, Hockenmaier (UIUC) | 2024-08 (v5 2025-12) | 3 (central) — the folder's audit instrument for the intervention itself rather than its finding: completeness (does the edit actually transform the property?) and selectivity (does it leave non-targeted properties alone?) are measured by validation probes trained on disjoint data and handed the edited embedding instead of the model, reliability is their harmonic mean, and every strength dial is swept rather than taken at one point. Result: all six methods trade completeness for selectivity in all six models and layers, nonlinear gradient interventions dominate at best-reliability settings (0.92-0.98 on GPT-2, Pythia, Llama; 0.938-0.943 on Pythia-160M) except on BERT where the linear AlterRep wins at 0.835, more reliable interventions cause larger accuracy drops, and the nonlinear-over-linear gap survives a linear-validation-probe control. Limits: subject-verb agreement with two binary properties plus an IOI replication, three methods on the two largest Pythias, linearity claim offered as conjecture. |

arxiv-2601.06305 | Why LoRA Fails to Forget: Regularized Low-Rank Adaptation Against Backdoors in Language Models | Luong & Chen (Rochester Institute of Technology) | 2026-01-09 | 2 (useful) — the weight-side counterpart to the folder's spectral-detector entry, and a mechanism rather than a detector: it argues that LoRA fails to undo a pretraining-time backdoor not because rank is small but because the update is spectrally weak (its top singular value sits below the pretrained layer's at every layer measured) and spectrally misaligned (small but nonzero cosine to the pretrained top directions). Linearised argument gives a scale threshold for when task dominance beats the trigger, and the rescaling sweep shows the threshold shape empirically. Defence: dropout on frozen weights + soft orthogonality to the pretrained subspaces + layerwise post-hoc rescale; attack success 99.70 → 7.48 (BERT/BadNet/SST-2), 2.31 (LLaMA/BadNet/SST-2), clean accuracy within a point or two, +6 to +15 ms per iteration. The valuable table is the ablation: orthogonality alone barely works (93.84 InSent/RoBERTa), dropout alone is the strong term, only the combination is reliable. Classic uncorrected cells left unchecked (InSent/CoLA 60.06 RoBERTa, 30.24 LLaMA) and a broken FFT row (77.63 ASR at 15.43 CA). Also: poisoned frozen models already score 75.84-86.19 downstream before any adaptation, a confound for every forgetting claim. Best numbers are best-of-several-runs, baselines partly copied from a prior paper, motivating spectra shown as figures only. Limits: no adaptive attack, moderate-scale models, linearised theory.

arxiv-2501.19271 | Concept-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence: Metrics & Benchmarks | Aysel, Cai & Prugel-Bennett (University of Southampton) | 2025-01-31 | 2 (useful) — the folder's first benchmark for scoring concept claims against independent annotation, split into three instruments: CGIM (cosine between the model's concept-by-class matrix and the annotated one), CEM (does the top-l concept exist in the image?) and CLM (does the concept's heatmap contain the annotated part centre?), plus CoAM, a concept-weighted analogue of a class activation map. Reproduced post-hoc CBMs on CUB-200 (ResNet-18, 112 concepts, 59.1% accuracy vs 75.4% bottleneck-free): the top concept is present only 49.3% of the time over the test set and 55.4% on correctly classified images when ranked by weight times projected value, but 84.3% when ranked by projected value alone — the unweighted read-out is systematically optimistic. Localisation is far worse: 13.3% at a twelfth-of-image region, 33.4% at a quarter, 59.0% at half. Global alignment is broadly distributed with a negative tail (black-eye-colour concept at cosine -0.63), attributed to concept co-occurrence. Limits: one dataset, one method family, CLM relies on a hand mapping of 112 concepts onto 12 body parts, CEM needs per-image labels almost no dataset has, and the localisation score measures the model plus a visualisation it was not designed for. |

arxiv-2405.06800 | LLM-Generated Black-box Explanations Can Be Adversarially Helpful | Ajwani, Javaji, Rudzicz & Zhu (Toronto / Vector / Stevens / UMass / Dalhousie) | 2024-05-10 | 2 (useful) — the natural-language half of the folder's description-scoring line: a black-box explainer asked to justify a *wrong* answer produces convincing, fluent, largely factually-correct prose that shifts readers toward it. Name for the failure: adversarial helpfulness. Humans (MTurk, 3-point scale, three raters per item) move from 2.96 to 3.53 (GPT-4, ECQA) / 3.66 to 3.72 (Claude) / 3.74 to 3.84 (Chat), all p<0.01; proxy LLM evaluators reproduce it only partly (Vicuna-33B and WizardLM-70B at p<0.001 corrected, Mixtral not at all, and Mixtral degenerate at 3.00 flat on NLI E->N). Ten-strategy taxonomy, GPT-4-Turbo detection: comparative-advantage framing in >70% of ECQA explanations (90/79/82), question-reframing in >90% of NLI (93-95), selective evidence 43-67; authority and analogy almost never. Structural test on linearised trees of B branches x L depth: success falls with complexity, and with randomised node names every model but GPT-4/4-Turbo drops to zero, GPT-4 failing nearly half at L=6 — the text is carried by lexical form, not graph navigation. Best methodological content is the authors' own §10: no item-level human-vs-proxy correlation is significant and every proxy pair agrees at Cohen's kappa < 0.1, so this is a worked example of significance without agreement. Missing control: no uninformative-explanation arm; no correct-answer arm; one prompt family per setting. |
