arxiv-2110.08260 | Abstract Interpretation of Fixpoint Iterators with Applications to Neural Networks | ETH Zurich (Mark Niklas Müller, Marc Fischer, Robin Staab, Martin Vechev) | 2023-04 | 2 - the folder's cleanest instance of ABSTRACTING THE ENDPOINT RATHER THAN THE TRAJECTORY: standard abstract interpretation keeps every reachable state because a loop might stop anywhere, but for a solver that converges to a UNIQUE fixpoint the stopping point is pinned by a mathematical invariant, so the paper never builds an abstract transformer for the termination test at all and never uses a join - instead it iterates a sound abstract solver step until the next abstract state is CONTAINED IN the current one, and Theorem 3.1 proves that this very containment implies the state contains every concrete fixpoint for the whole input region (one step into itself means no number of concrete steps escapes, and the concrete iteration converges in finitely many steps); a second theorem yields the weaker property that lets stage two keep tightening beyond the containment point - any sound abstraction of a locally Lipschitz iterator with a unique convergent fixpoint maps an over-approximation of the fixpoint set to another one (fixpoint set preservation), with a wider parameter range proved for forward-backward splitting; THE ROOT CAUSE OF EVERY NUMBER IS THE INCLUSION CHECK, not the per-step description - containment must be cheap and the outer object must be proper, so they invent a hybrid zonotope with an INVERTIBLE error matrix plus a consolidation operator that compresses any number of error terms back to exactly the latent dimension on a PCA basis, which makes containment a matrix inequality instead of a general zonotope test (the standard general-zonotope approximate check runs 500s to 2000s per check at the smallest 40-dimensional setting against a check that is 1.8 per cent less precise and more than four orders of magnitude faster); the deliberately COUNTER-INTUITIVE move is to EXPAND the abstraction while searching for containment, and the paper explicitly distinguishes this from widening - widening terminates an increasing chain, expansion breaks a stall between INCOMPARABLE sets - and removing it loses half the samples outright (post-fixpoint found on 50 of 100 instead of 100, certified 9 instead of 30); THE ABLATION TO REMEMBER is 'same iteration containment': requiring the state used for the final certificate to also be contained in its predecessor certifies 0 of 100 samples, which is the paper's own proof that the weaker second-stage guarantee is what makes the analysis work, and the box-only domain is the mirror image - it converges on all 100 samples in 0.38s per sample and certifies NONE, i.e. the fastest and most complete iteration is worthless because the answer is too loose to decide anything; against the semidefinite state of the art on the two small latents (the only size its solver permits) Craft is 3-4 orders of magnitude faster at the smallest radius (~1s vs 401.5s/1388.1s) and MORE precise at larger ones (36 vs 18 at radius 0.05 on the 40-wide latent, 30 vs 24 on the 87-wide), and it reaches latents of 200, 648 and 800 and CIFAR10 at 2/255 that the SDP approach cannot touch, with the surprise that the CONVOLUTIONAL monDEQs are easier to certify than the fully connected ones; 82.8 per cent of the collision-avoidance input region certified globally by exhaustive splitting, with an uncertifiable boundary band and a small uncertifiable interior pocket; on the square-root case study Kleene iteration diverges to an unbounded interval where Craft stays tight; limits named: contraction is not guaranteed even for exact abstractions and the incomplete check can miss it, and the over-approximated iteration is not guaranteed to converge - plus, unraised, that the expansion and splitting parameters came from coarse manual search. arxiv-2108.00893 | Static analysis of ReLU neural networks with tropical polyhedra | LIX, Ecole Polytechnique / CNRS / Institut Polytechnique de Paris + University of Colorado Boulder (Goubault, Palumby, Sankaranarayanan, Putot, Rustenholz) | 2021-08 | 2 - the folder's first account whose ABSTRACT DOMAIN IS CHOSEN TO MATCH THE FUNCTION rather than the geometry around it: a ReLU net computes a rational map in the max-plus (tropical) semiring, so the authors abstract it with tropical polyhedra, and the resulting asymmetry is the whole paper - the ReLU is EXACT in that algebra (apply it coordinatewise to the generators, no error at all) while the ordinary affine layer is the only place conservatism enters, handled by computing the tightest ZONE containing the graph of the affine map over the input box and then rewriting that zone as the tropical convex hull of n+1 explicit generators (a theorem with both directions proved); an octagon lift then adds sum-type constraints by duplicating each variable into positive and negative copies and intersecting the tropical polyhedron with the linear manifold that pins the two copies to be negatives; multilayering is embedding + intersection + projection, with the non-obvious internal-route theorem that embedding into a larger space does NOT cost 2^k generators - you keep the old generators at the lower bound plus only those that are not absorbable under max-plus at the upper bound; THE ARGUMENT BY PICTURE IS THE PART TO REMEMBER: on a two-input toy, every classically convex abstraction must extend the true cyan range up to its convex hull, and that hull intersects the unsafe region, so the property is unprovable, while the tropical polyhedron reproduces the graph exactly and rejects the counterexample region - the domain wins not by being tighter in general but by refusing the closure; precision is then bought by SUBDIVIDING the input box, where the same toy's projected area goes 2.5x the exact range before subdivision, 1.5x after two sub-intervals and 1.25x after four; THE FAILURE IS PRINTED IN THE SAME PAPER and is the sharpest thing in it - the 'multi' net's seven true [0,2] output ranges come back as [0,6],[0,4],[0,4],[0,2],[0,4],[0,2],[0,2] because a zone-based tropical abstraction tracks DIFFERENCES of neuron values but cannot express SUMS, so z1+z2<=2 is simply outside the constraint language (their krelu comparison says a competitor's multi-neuron ReLU abstraction does get it); cost is brutal and honest - the C++ internal route is 0.005-0.2s on the Sherlock controllers (0.75s at 105 neurons, 88.8s and 104.75s at 506) while the polymake double-description route runs 1.83s to 1682s on the same objects, and the conclusion states the account is usable when you commit to EITHER the internal OR the external representation, 'not both at the same time'; property checking is only implemented in the form that reduces to an LP over the enclosing zone, so the polyhedron's own extra precision is not yet exploited; a preliminary prototype on small nets with no shared-benchmark comparison against other verifiers. arxiv-2410.23903 | Neural Network Verification with PyRAT | CEA (Lemesle, Lehmann, Le Gall) | 2025-09 | 2 - THE DOMAIN INVENTORY, and its shape is the empirical form of the folder's question: practitioners do not pick one abstraction per network, they STACK them - the cheap interval box is always on, not because it is tight but because it is EXACT at the ReLU layer (an increasing function on an interval is just the function of its endpoints), so every relational domain is intersected with it layer by layer and even the branch-and-bound splits are applied by adding constraints to the constrained zonotope rather than by narrowing the box; four domains are described along one ladder of precision and cost - boxes (error is O(d), and x-x on [-1,1] gives [-2,2], the elementary statement that intervals see no relation), zonotopes (a weighted Minkowski sum over noise symbols, exact for every affine/convex layer, one fresh noise symbol per unstable ReLU via the DeepZ linearisation, with heuristics that MERGE noise symbols once a budget is hit so the O(m*d) cost stays bounded at a known precision loss), constrained zonotopes (the same object plus K inequality constraints shared over all dimensions, two constraints y>=x and y>=0 per unstable ReLU, whose tightest box comes from a Lagrangian DUAL maximised by SGD/Adam instead of a constraint-programming solver precisely because every lambda gives a valid bound and the solvers are not sound in real arithmetic), and hybrid zonotopes (union of constrained zonotopes through binary symbols, which represent a piecewise-linear network EXACTLY and transfer all difficulty to a MILP); THE SCALING LAW IS THE RESULT: hybrid zonotopes prove all four mooring-line properties in 6.28s, over ten times faster than any branch-and-bound route, then prove 11 of 60 on LinearizeNN (worse than constrained zonotopes), 22 of 186 on ACAS-Xu (worst in that table) and TIMEOUT ON EVERY CIFAR-100 PROPERTY, while plain constrained zonotopes with ReLU branching go from 8 proven without branching to 32 on CIFAR-100 - exactness is a small-network instrument and branch-and-bound is the large-network one; the branching choice is a RATIO RULE worth carrying: split INPUTS when the input dimension is small relative to unstable-ReLU count (58 of 60 proven on LinearizeNN at 123s versus 19 at 2521s for ReLU splitting) and split RELUs when inputs are high-dimensional (input splitting proves ZERO extra properties on CIFAR-100), with the node chosen by a first-order influence estimate that multiplies the domain's input-output coefficients by the box width (or, for ReLUs, by the effect of pinning the node, computed from gradients for polyhedra); FOREVER WATCH THE COLUMN SEMANTICS - the falsified count is a PRECISION statistic, not an error statistic, and it moves the opposite way from what a reader expects (sharper domains and more sub-problems find MORE counterexamples: 0 falsified with plain zonotopes and 13 with constrained zonotopes on ACAS-Xu, then 45-47 with input branching), so collapsing proven/falsified/unknown/timeout into one number would invert the sign of the conclusion; on the large benchmark fewer than half of 100 properties are settled at all; against alpha-beta-CROWN PyRAT is fast on small instances but carries about 500 extra timeouts, 400 of them on genuinely SAFE properties, and the paper names the cause (branch-and-bound heuristics on high-dimensional inputs) rather than the domain; and soundness is a MODE not a property - real-arithmetic soundness is achieved by forcing the most pessimistic rounding on every operation and is UNAVAILABLE on GPU and in fast modes, so a timing wins a premise; five industrial deployments (Airbus int8 quantised nets with an ED-324/ARP6983 certification route, 224x224 classifiers at 95 per cent accuracy proving over 90 per cent of the test set locally robust, CAISAR, the TRUMPET medical project) and the soundness benchmark on which it is one of two tools assessed correct. arxiv-2007.06093 | Interval Universal Approximation for Neural Networks | University of Wisconsin-Madison + CUHK (Wang, Albarghouthi, Prakriya, Jha) | 2021-07 | 2 - THE IMPOSSIBILITY SIDE OF THE ABSTRACT-INTERPRETATION LADDER, and the cleanest one-sentence statement of the ceiling the last five runs have been circling: for ANY continuous function on a compact box and ANY tolerance there EXISTS a network, using ANY of what the authors call squashable activations (their canonical form: a bounded monotone function, which covers sigmoid, tanh, softsign directly and ReLU, ELU, softplus, smooth ReLU via one uniform round-trip construction), whose INTERVAL abstract interpretation lands within delta of the function's true set semantics for every input box - and yet NO efficient construction of such a network exists, because approximating a network's range to a tolerance below one half is NP-hard AND coNP-hard and Delta-2-intermediate for polynomial-time networks with finite precision, while above one half it is trivial (return the midpoint); THE DICHOTOMY IS THE RESULT TO KEEP: the hardness is not on a gradient, it flips at exactly delta = 1/2, so 'the instrument can be as precise as you like' and 'you can find the instrument' are two wholly different claims and only the first is true - and a good POINTWISE approximator of f does not hand you an interval approximator of it, so this is genuinely not a corollary of classical universal approximation; the construction is a grid at spacing epsilon, a cell indicator built as the difference of two half-cell-shifted dilated copies of the activation (dilation chosen from the LIMIT definition so the 0-to-1 transition is forced inside half a cell), the m-dimensional indicator a sum of per-dimension indicators shifted so any single out-of-neighbourhood dimension forces the sum negative, then the function sliced into horizontal bands of height delta/3 (finer than the predecessor's delta/2, precisely to absorb the extra imprecision from arbitrary activations) summed and rescaled, with the whole proof closed by an explicit nested-interval inequality; the ERROR ACCOUNTING inside that proof is a template worth lifting - almost all precision loss is localised to the two bands straddling the function's minimum and maximum, every other band is shown near-exact, and the disjunction over dimensions is handled by a counting budget (theta bounded by the reciprocal of the dimension count and the grid size) so the sum cannot drift; cost is stated plainly at 2m+1 activation units, depth 2, width 2m for one cell indicator, 4m+2 ReLU neurons against a predecessor's 10m-3, and the ReLU falsification hardness result falls out as a corollary via the same 3CNF-to-network gadget; THE LIMIT THE PAPER STATES ITSELF is the one that matters for us: the interval domain is NON-RELATIONAL, so the multi-class extension has to zero out every non-predicted class before the theorem applies, because an interval cannot express which output is larger - the exact weakness entry chained abstract domains to route around; no experiment, no benchmark, no dataset, no baseline, no code anywhere, every number a constant in a proof. arxiv-2212.07553 | Automated Reachability Analysis of Neural Network-Controlled Systems via Adaptive Polytopes | Johns Hopkins University | 2023-05-15 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v3, ~50k chars; abstract, §1-§2, §3 with Algorithm 1 and both proofs, §4, Table 1, Fig. 3-4 captions; no discussion or limitations section exists). Closed-loop reachability of an affine plant with a ReLU controller, where the set representation is the lever: the “wrapping effect” is the error you get when a summary is fed back into its own input. Their fix is structural - rewrite x⁺ = Ax + Bf(x) + e as one skip-free ReLU net by the identity that a vector is the difference of its positive and negative parts, which removes the Minkowski sum of plant image and controller image, then compute each step's offsets by branch and bound on the UNROLLED map from the initial box, so step k's enclosure never depends on step k-1's enclosure. Directions are derived rather than chosen: facet normals pulled back through the pseudo-inverse (C ← C W†), orthogonal-complement directions ±u_i added when a layer widens (output provably has zero variance there), -e_i added after every layer for the rectifier clip, cosine-similarity λ=0.98 dedup to cap facet count; proved to stay a bounded polytope and to be TIGHT in the widening case. Numbers: quadrotor 12 steps - theirs 213.67 s / 0.501 s per problem, ReachLP-GSG 18.8 s / 0.13, ReachLipBnB 2170 s / 11.3, ReachLP-uniform timed out at 27 h; double integrator - theirs slowest in total (9.96 s vs 1.078 s) at 0.134 s/problem. The totals mislead because each arm solves a different number of sub-problems (74 and 426 total vs a fixed few per step), so per-problem is the only fair column. Limits (conclusion only): partitioning is over the input set so cost is exponential in state dimension; they name less conservative propagators, activation-space branching, operator splitting. Unmeasured: how much tightness is the directions vs the unrolling; λ is a free knob. Pure theory note: reachability for a discrete-time loop of (ReLU feedforward controller, plant) is UNDECIDABLE, and it survives a plant that just returns the control vector (P(x,u)=u), integer weights, a singleton initial set and a target pinning one output coordinate - witnesses: 6 hidden layers at 3 inputs / 3 outputs, or ONE wide hidden layer via seven parallel tracks plus a modulo-7 counter that gates liveness, paying in width. Method: two-counter-machine gadgets, one per instruction, all evaluated in parallel with a program-counter match spike selecting the live one and a fixed offset subtracted at the output; the plant is the identity, so hardness rides entirely on the feedback edge. Positive side: SEMI-decidable when plant + initial + target sets are omega-regular (Büchi automata over bit-pair reals, network graph encoded and modified to echo its input so it composes), iterating I_k = I_{k-1} o_d (N o_{d+c} P) and testing nonemptiness - and this is tight, since the identity plant is omega-regular. Multi-mode linear maps (rational flow per mode, disjoint-and-covering guards, fixed rational period) shown omega-regular, hence covered. No implementation, no benchmark, no timing. arxiv-1906.10654 | ReachNN: Reachability Analysis of Neural-Network Controlled Systems | Northwestern University / Boston University / University of Dayton | 2019-06-25 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~79k chars; abstract, §1-§6 plus Tables 1-2 and Figures 3-6 captions and §5 discussion; reference list only after §6). The canonical constructive single-step method for the closed loop, kept general by giving up tightness: replace the controller with a Bernstein polynomial fitted on the step box, plus a CERTIFIED error box, then integrate the plant with Flow* - so the surrogate keeps state-variable dependencies that an interval destroys. Two error routes: T-error = a layer-by-layer Lipschitz estimate (activation-derivative bound over the actual interval, which beats the naive weight-norm product) times the published Bernstein rate for Lipschitz functions; S-error = grid-cell centre discrepancy plus a Lipschitz term proportional to cell diagonal, so the grid spacing PAYS for the soundness claim, and the grid is auto-sized to a sampling-precision target. Sampling study: same box, Bernstein fit error orders of magnitude apart (ReLU ~1e-12 vs smooth ~1e-4), unexplained. Lipschitz experiment: controller with constant 874.5 loses the bound at step 10; retrained to 14.7 with a product-of-spectral-norms penalty it holds for 20 steps with comparable behaviour - verifiability is a property of the controller, not just the method. arxiv-2304.03671 | Contraction-Guided Adaptive Partitioning for Reachability Analysis of Neural Network Controlled Systems | Georgia Tech ECE (Harapanahalli, Jafarpour, Coogan) | 2023-04-07 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~74k chars; abstract, §I-§VII, Algorithm 1 line by line, Thm 1 with Grönwall proof, Thm 2 contraction-rate bound, Tables I and II). Partitioning driven by a LOCAL MEASURED RATE instead of a global constant: push the mixed-monotone closed-loop embedding to a fraction gamma of the control interval, take the width ratio as that partition's empirical contraction rate, and if the projected width at interval end still exceeds the target epsilon, REWIND to the interval start and bisect into 2^n sub-boxes (so the over-wide box is never carried forward). Two independent depth budgets make the separation real - plant integration at every leaf, the CROWN network enclosure cached and INHERITED down the tree until a network-depth cap - so accuracy is bought without new verifier calls, and parents are the tightest box over their children's enclosures rather than a chain of Minkowski sums. Theory turns the measurement into a promise: enclosure error <= decaying initial-set width term + network-bound-gap term + disturbance term, all scaled by the embedding's contraction rate c_x, with c_x bounded above by the plant's open-loop rate plus (plant-input gain x network Lipschitz constant); negative c_x means the initial-set error vanishes. Double integrator (2-10-5 ReLU net): 7.5e-3 final area in 0.83 s versus 1.2e-2 in 3.68 s for the best listed baseline; looser setting 1.0e-1 area in 0.079 s. Vehicle (4x100x100x2 net, 1.25 s horizon): adaptive 1.24-1.58 s versus 1.85 s non-adaptive at depth 1, 2.64-3.33 s versus 4.27 s at depth 2, tightest volume 1.689 at epsilon=0.2. Guarantees are proved for a CONTINUOUSLY applied controller while the runs use zero-order hold; the cached enclosure may have been certified on a LARGER box than the partition using it, and that loss is not reported. arxiv-2304.01218 | POLAR-Express: Efficient and Precise Formal Reachability Analysis of Neural-Network Controlled Systems | Boston U. / Northwestern / Univ. Dayton / Univ. Liverpool | 2023-03 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~93k chars; abstract, S I-VI, Algorithms 1-5, Lemma 1-2, Thm 1, Table III in full). Engineered successor to the same authors' prototype, and the first paper in the closed-loop thread that compares families rather than methods. Two families: range-only tools (per-step network output enclosure + plant reachability) versus dependency-tracking tools (functional enclosure of the whole flowmap). POLAR-Express is the latter: Taylor/Bernstein polynomials plus interval remainders propagated layer by layer, with three additions - (1) choose Taylor or Bernstein AFTER composition, with a worked sigmoid counterexample showing the smaller standalone residual can compose to the larger one (they define this as the 'accuracy preservation problem' and answer it no); (2) for convex activations, notably ReLU, the Bernstein polynomial is one-sided, so the upper bound is the polynomial and the lower bound is the same polynomial minus its value at zero, a remainder they prove tight for any order; (3) remainders kept SYMBOLIC with the accumulated transforming matrix and collapsed to an interval only at the output layer, buying tighter boxes at quadratic (not linear) depth cost. 16 benchmark configurations vs 6 tools: proves every standard reach-avoid case (never U), quadrotor-MPC safe in 13.1 s vs 961.4 s for Verisig 2.0 and U after 10854 s for the range-only stack, QUAD20 (12-dim, 20 agents) done in 316.8 + 212.5 s where others fail at 1 step or explode at 25. Rectifier example 1.8 s vs 7.1 s for the predecessor. No width ratio anywhere - tightness is read off overlaid plots; authors document competitor-side confounds (CORA sets missing simulated traces on 2 of 16, a warm-run timing default, a div-by-zero crash). Scaling attributed to state dimension, step size and horizon, all outside the method. arxiv-2407.14394 | TTT: A Temporal Refinement Heuristic for Tenuously Tractable Discrete Time Reachability Problems | KTH Royal Institute of Technology (Sidrane, Tumova) | 2024-07-19 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~38k chars; abstract, §I-§VII, Algorithms 1-2, Appendices, Figs 4-6 tables). The TEMPORAL side of refinement, as opposed to the spatial side every other paper in this thread works on: instead of tuning the set representation or the partition, choose WHEN along the horizon to fire expensive multi-step symbolic queries (whose intermediate sets implicitly constrain trajectories passing through them) versus cheap one-step concrete ones. Two phases - SEARCH raises the symbolic depth one at a time from the initial set until a crude per-step cost estimate (time just spent divided by steps just covered, running max) says one more depth would eat the whole budget, then JUMP walks the rest of the horizon in equal-sized symbolic jumps chosen so the horizon divides evenly, with a hand-tuned early-stop watchdog shrinking the jump by one if the MILP has no feasible solution yet. Underlying engine (piecewise-linear bounds on the nonlinear dynamics + rectified network encoded as an MILP + hyperrectangular template) is INHERITED unchallenged and soundness is asserted by citation, so the contribution lives entirely on the heuristic side. Chain: pendulum 2x25 -> 15.3s vs 19.3s hand-tuned (20.9% faster), volume-error 1.94 vs 2.27; TORA 3x25 -> 47.8s vs 63.0s (24%), volume-error 7.78 vs 7.67 which is 1.2% WORSE; car 1x100 -> 117s vs 400s (70.8%, 4.7 min), volume 3.89 vs 4.90; car 1x200 -> 131s vs 378s (65.2%, 4.1 min), volume 4.43 vs 5.29. Naive one-step baseline is far worse on everything (car volume 37.7). Given longer than the baseline's own runtime, pendulum error drops ~40% further. Error is a RATIO OF SUMMED VOLUMES (with summed radii as a second metric) printed beside every runtime - the slack number this thread has been missing. No monotonicity guarantee (bigger budget does not imply tighter set), no completeness/convergence, budget promise only approximate because the cost model is not an upper bound. arxiv-1802.06981 | Reachable Set Estimation and Safety Verification for Piecewise Linear Systems with Neural Network Controllers | Vanderbilt ECE (Xiang, Tran, Rosenfeld, Johnson) | 2018-02-20 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, 48,672 bytes; abstract, §I-§V, Algorithms 1-3, References [1]-[21]). The exact-representation ancestor of the region-enumeration line: the layer map is derived by splitting on the sign pattern of the preactivations, 2^n patterns per layer with the all-off and all-on extremes handled separately and the middle 2^n-2 written in one indicator-matrix formula, so a rectified layer maps a union of polytopes to a union of polytopes EXACTLY (three-case proof, plus a linear-output-layer corollary and a composition corollary). Closed loop is then one network pushforward plus one linear plant map per time step (Algorithm 3, exact). Union count multiplies per step and is called intractable, so a convex-hull variant carries one polytope per step and over-approximates (Corollary 3). Example: 2 modes in the plane with periodic switching, 2-layer 4-hidden/2-output net, random weights, unit box initial set, 400 trajectories on a 0.1 grid plotted over the computed region; [0,5] clear of the unsafe box near (4,4) -> safe, [0,10] touches it -> uncertain even though no sampled trajectory enters it. NO polytope count, NO runtime, NO width/volume ratio, NO tool comparison - validation is a picture overlay and the verdict is read off the figures. Two-and-a-half-valued verdict vocabulary (safe vs uncertain, no promotion without a witness) is the weak ancestor of the three-valued verdict in 630. arxiv-2405.18554 | Scalable Surrogate Verification of Image-based NNCS using Composition and Unrolling | Stony Brook / Clemson / MIT | 2024-05-28 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, 72,676 chars clean; abstract, S I-VI, Algorithms 1-2, Fig.8 cell counts, Table I architectures, Table III runtimes). The SURROGATE-VERIFICATION branch of the closed-loop thread, and the cleanest case in the folder of slack decomposed by CAUSE rather than reported as a number. Baseline replaces the camera with a cGAN, composes generator+controller into one net, asks a verifier for control intervals per state cell, then applies monotone plant analysis - two named error sources: one-step (coupling between state and command is discarded by the interval) and multi-step (reachable set snapped to grid cells every step, error compounds). Two remedies: COMPOSITION folds the plant into the same composed net (as an extra layer when the verifier supports tan - which fails outright because an interval containing the tangent pole has unbounded output; or via star-set exact analysis + conservative Taylor linearisation with interval Lagrange remainder), and UNROLLING composes m control periods into one net so snapping happens once per m steps, with the 1..m-1 step computations kept for soundness and a backward fixed-point variant. Taxiing: single-cell successors 18 -> 13 -> from a cell, 55 baseline / 40 one-step / 25 two-step cells; converged set 661 / 383 / 240 cells, baseline steady state 175% larger. Braking (conv): one-step proves ZERO safe cells, two-step 384, three-step 2669, 3868 inconclusive; dropping control frequency 20->10->5 Hz makes the controller worse but cuts inconclusive from 38.7% to 7.4% to 3.5%. Transformer net: 5707 safe, 7.8% inconclusive. Cost table is honest and brutal: taxiing 51.16 h -> 3954.77 h (1->2 steps); braking 125.14 -> 374.26 h; transformer 2630.88 -> 3609.23 h. No composition-vs-unrolling ablation; limitations section is entirely about cGAN fidelity, not about the analysis. arxiv-2207.02715 | Open- and Closed-Loop Neural Network Verification using Polynomial Zonotopes | Stony Brook / Aalborg / TU Munich | 2022-07 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, 63,033 chars clean; abstract, §1-§7, Algorithms 1-2, Props 1-2 with Appendix A proof, Tables 1-2 in full). The NON-CONVEX-representation branch of the closed-loop thread, and the ancestor of the quadratic per-neuron abstraction: each neuron's transfer curve is replaced by a degree-2 polynomial (closed-form for ReLU with value+slope pinned at the lower end and matched at the upper; least squares on N=10 points, which beats Taylor for sigmoid/tanh; Taylor expansion) and the polynomial is propagated through a sparse polynomial zonotope, which is CLOSED under polynomial maps - so no sign-pattern splitting, no unions, no case analysis, and the exponential of pattern enumeration is replaced by a generator-count growth handled by one order-reduction call per layer. Residue handled by adding a box equal to max/min of (activation minus quadratic) on the interval - exact min/max for ReLU via the split at zero and the quadratic vertex, and for sigmoid/tanh by sampling at spacing set from globally bounded derivatives with a user precision of 0.001. Closed loop: Cartesian product of reachable set and input set that DELIBERATELY PRESERVES shared dependent scalars (Prop. 2, cheap only because both sets come from the same trajectory), then conservative polynomialization integration of the extended state+input system. Image tightness shown only as overlays vs zonotope/star-set/Taylor/it. Open-loop: 5 ACAS Xu net-spec pairs at 0.53/0.16/0.35/0.19/0.54 s vs 13 competition tools (times taken from the public VNN-COMP results repo, not re-run), fast on all five but its own splitting takes 34.1 s and 40.6 s on two of them. Closed-loop: faster than all other tools on all but one of 8 benchmark families (Sherlock/JuliaReach/Verisig/Verisig2.0/ReachNN*, times lifted from those papers' own tables), attributed to tightness letting coarse integrator settings and no set splitting. NO width ratio, NO generator count, NO ablation, NO limitations section - slack is available per neuron structurally and still not printed. arxiv-2211.11127 | BBReach: Tight and Scalable Black-Box Reachability Analysis of DRL Systems | ECNU / ETH Zurich / Oxford / Hebrew University | 2022-11-21 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, ~69k chars clean; abstract, S1-S6, Algorithms 1-2, Lemmas 1-2 + Thm 4.1 proofs, Table 1 in full, Appendices 0.A-0.D). The paper in this thread that MOVES THE COST INTO TRAINING instead of into the analysis: the policy network is retrained with the abstraction function as input layer, so it is constant on every grid cell by construction, which licenses treating the network as a black box and asking it ONCE PER CELL for a single action - no interval, no relaxation, NO network over-approximation at all, so the network's size/shape/activation stops mattering (4x200 nets cost about the same as 3x100). Analysis is then: cut each reachable box along the abstraction grid (interval segmentation) so every piece lies in one cell, bound the one-step successor per dimension by a max/min of the dynamics with the action fixed, then MERGE adjacent boxes (min bounding rectangle) to keep the count flat. Adjacent relation has three forms (inclusion / overlap in exactly one dimension within threshold h / separation in exactly one dimension within h); merge assumes adjacency is TRANSITIVE (stated assumption, not proved) and uses a prebuilt adjacency matrix + BFS connected components to go from brute-force O(n^3) to O(n^2). Soundness: Lemma 1 (post per box), Lemma 2 (every box in X is inside its merged box), Thm 4.1 by induction on trajectory length. Results, 7 RL tasks dim 2-6 x 4 nets (tanh/reLU x sizes) = 28 instances: BBReach verifies ALL 28 vs 12 for Verisig 2.0 and 13 for ReachNN* (which return 1 and 11 'unknown'); but the competitors are simply N/A on the 7 ReLU instances (Verisig 2.0 cannot do ReLU), so much of the headline is a COVERAGE win not a tightness win. Times: 20-core mostly sub-second to a few s, Tora (dim 4) 44.25 s / 814.3 s on 1 core; size-invariance is the load-bearing result. Tightness explicitly COMPARABLE on most benchmarks, better on ACC (6-dim, sample-based tool blows up), and WORSE than Verisig 2.0 on B2 - attributed to the two nets having learned different routes (their system differs), not to their method being looser. Ablation that is the cleanest number: box count vs step grows fast with no aggregation, stays 'extremely small and stable' with it; over-approximation + aggregation dominate runtime, segmentation negligible; cost FALLS and then PLATEAUS as granularity coarsens. The comparison runs the competitors on DIFFERENT networks for the same task (retrained, and small weights chosen because Verisig 2.0 degrades with big ones - Appendix 0.A). Four-way verdict vocabulary (verified/unknown/DNF/N-A) is the honest minimum. No limitations section, no code link, no compute statement beyond the workstation spec (32-core Threadripper, 128GB). arxiv-2110.01388 | Neural Network Verification in Control | MIT (Aerospace Controls Lab) | 2021-09-30 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, clean body except IV-D/IV-E garble). Tutorial that UNIFIES the thread's shelved literature into one architecture with three named roles: ANALYZER owns the output shape and the stopping rule, PARTITIONER splits the input set, PROPAGATOR bounds each cell (IBP / CROWN affine envelope / QP-SDP), and every analysis problem in the paper is one scalar objective over the same per-layer constraints (reachability, yes/no verification, minimal adversarial example). Two claims that matter for us: (1) the two paradigms were built separately toward the same goal and nesting them is what makes a method tight enough for a feedback loop - the greedy simulation-guided partitioner re-picks which cell to refine every iteration (furthest image outside the Monte-Carlo hull), reducing to plain CROWN at iteration 0 with 1 propagator call and reaching 29 calls by iteration 14; (2) for a loop, bounding the control then applying it at extreme states is qualitatively worse than optimising the next-state facet jointly, which is why the two separate-analysis rows of Table II sit far above the four joint rows. Closed-loop result is a SINGLE double integrator with a 5x5 ReLU policy: CL-CROWN 0.000/65,455; CL-SG-IBP 0.888/70,218; Reach-SDP 42.57/207; Reach-SDP-Partition 670.26/12; Reach-LP 0.017/1,590; Reach-LP-Partition 0.263/34 (runtime s / error) - caption arithmetic calls the last ~5x tighter AND ~150x faster than Reach-SDP, and the unpartitioned LP ~4,000x faster but ~7x looser. The error column IS a slack ratio (sampled AABB area divided by provided-set area, minus one) - so the reporting discipline the thread spent runs 626-640 looking for appears here, in a TUTORIAL, with a sample-based denominator; and the figure prose admits tightness degrades with horizon for every method. Isolated-NN tightness is eye-only (six panels, 2 s budget, judged against a sampled hull). RL third: CARRL takes argmax of the per-action WORST-CASE Q lower bound instead of emitting a sensitivity flag - three named structural differences from SL certification (a flag cannot be acted on, no correct label exists, actions change the future). Names partitioning's hard limit: worst case grows as 2 to the input dimension, viable only when uncertainty sits on a few dims. arxiv-2211.03732 | Approximating Reachable Sets for Neural Network based Models in Real-Time via Optimal Control | Purdue University | 2022-11-07 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, clean, all sections present). The folder's first genuinely BLACK-BOX member of the closed-loop thread: the plant is a learned 12-DOF quadrotor multistep MLP (12/256/12, tanh, 100 trajectories, MSE 1.26e-3) and the analyser never reads a weight, instead exciting the NN with commands, stacking 8-wide input-state snapshots and solving a least-squares DMD-with-control pseudo-inverse at every step to get an LTV pair (A_k,B_k), then running CLASSICAL support-hyperplane reachability (Pontryagin costate propagation; 24 initial-set hyperplanes, 8 input-set hyperplanes; 0.1 s steps, 5 s horizon) on the surrogate. Same computation yields BOTH an inner approximation (convex hull of propagated contact points) and an outer one (half-space intersection) so the tightness gap the thread spent runs 626-641 asking for is constructed here for free - and never printed, never plotted, never compared, which makes this the strongest case yet that the reporting gap is about incentives not instrumentation. Second experiment (2 rotors failed -> input set becomes bounded noise) is a controlled error-budget demonstration: surrogate stays close to the LEARNED MODEL while both drift from truth, i.e. the reachable set encloses the model's set and not the world - the negative result is the paper's most useful line. Cost story is asymptotic only (O(1) in layers vs O(L) for LP/MILP, O(n^3) per hyperplane, exp[.] from matrix exponentiation) plus a single '<0.5 s per step' claim, no runtime sweep, no accuracy-vs-data curve (deferred to future work), no baseline implementation run. The transferable finding for us: the field's 'sound vs cheap' axis has a third coordinate, WHITE-BOX ACCESS, and the whole family's per-neuron/per-sign-pattern/per-generator cost structure is priced in that currency; this paper is what the ablation WITHOUT the white box looks like. arxiv-1805.09944 | Reachability Analysis and Safety Verification for Neural Network Control Systems | Vanderbilt University (Xiang, Johnson) | 2018-05-25 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, clean, all sections present). The documented ANCESTOR of the closed-loop thread's box-propagation default, and the first paper here to say out loud why the field's later members exist: enclosure-by-grid is SOUND and costs nothing per box, but its ONLY fidelity dial is an integer grid vector whose cardinality is a product over input dimensions. Mechanism: input set -> tightest axis-aligned box -> regular grid with M_i cuts per dim (empty cells dropped) -> per-cell, per-layer interval enclosure that is correct under a MONOTONE activation (min and max of the pre-activation pinned to the cell's corners, then activation applied to both) -> those LP problems collapse to a closed form (multiply by the low or high end depending on the weight's sign) -> union of output boxes. Gaussian activations handled by a four-case split around the peak (monotone up, monotone down, straddling with the peak as the max). Closed loop = alternate the network routine with an ODE reachability routine the paper explicitly does NOT reimplement; safety = set-intersection test returning SAFE or UNCERTAIN (never UNSAFE). Results: 7-unit tanh net, 10x10 to 50x50 grids -> 100 to 2500 boxes, 0.062 s to 0.383 s, 5000 sampled outputs inside the set at every resolution; 2-state plant + 5-unit net over 10 steps, grids of 5 and 20, 1000 sampled trajectories inside, coarser grid already clears the unsafe box so the verdict is resolution-insensitive here. No baseline, no tool comparison, no tightness metric beyond overlay figures, no limitations section. The transferable facts for us: (1) per-cell box propagation from the weights alone is a free LOWER bound on tightness that any region-granularity account should be measured against, reported as boxes-at-fixed-tightness rather than seconds; (2) the cost is grid-dominated and depth-insensitive, which is exactly the property later members trade away when they buy tightness with per-layer work. arxiv-2301.07531 | Safety Verification of Neural Network Control Systems Using Guaranteed Neural Network Model Reduction | Xiang, Shao (Augusta U / Southwest Jiaotong) | 2023-01 | 2 - model reduction certified by a reachability query on an augmented difference network; global scalar precision reused per step
arxiv-2309.03846 | Scalable Forward Reachability Analysis of Multi-Agent Systems with Neural Network Controllers | University of Oxford (Engineering Science) | 2023-09-07 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, clean, all sections present). The thread's first COMPOSITIONAL member, and its contribution is not a tighter bound but a cheaper enumeration: M agents each with their own ReLU controller read self+neighbour states, so instead of stacking every agent into one 4n-dim state and paying Reach-SDP's cost on the whole thing, each agent keeps its own small SDP whose input box is self+neighbour states. The enabling device is pure bookkeeping and is the reusable part: per-neighbour MLPs are FOLDED into ONE MLP over the concatenated self+neighbour state by block-diagonalising the first-layer weights (blkdiag over neighbours) between a broadcast selector that copies the agent's own block to every branch and a summing selector on the output - so a distributed architecture becomes an ordinary MLP and every single-net method applies unchanged. Saturation is absorbed as two extra ReLU layers so control limits live INSIDE the network, not in the analyser - the same 'put the restriction where the algebra can see it' move as runs 626/627. Uncertainty handled by requiring the LMI to hold at every vertex of a convex hull of (A,B) pairs, valid because the reachable-set matrix is affine in them - a finite-vertex enumeration, i.e. run 629's 'cost follows which structure you enumerate' applied to model space rather than state space. Numbers: platoon (9 vehicles, 2x15 ReLU nets, 0.1s ZOH, 5 steps) and 4-area AGC power network (2x10 nets, 1s ZOH, 3 steps); Table I M=1..5 gives 3.85/7.04/11.60/14.17/20.82 s vs reach-SDP 4.01/75.39/562.94/3636.62/41025.05 s - i.e. near-parity at M=1 and ~2000x at M=5, a GROWTH-LAW change not a constant factor, and worth noting that the speedup is exponential in M because the monolithic problem's LMI dimension grows with total state while the per-agent one does not. Critical gap for us: the authors assert the bounds are THE SAME but print no volume, no gap, no independent tool, no containment test - so the paper sells the decomposition and merely promises the equivalence, and the one number that would make it a result (bound width) is absent exactly as in runs 632/634/641/642. arxiv-2408.08592 | Case Study: Runtime Safety Verification of Neural Network Controlled System | Northwestern University / University of Southampton (Yang, Zhan, Wang, Huang, Zhu) | 2024-08-16 | 2 - full text (arXiv HTML v1, clean, all sections present). The closed-loop thread's first RUNTIME member: reachability is not asked once but called per tick inside a ROS2 Flatland control loop, so the thread's fidelity dial (how many steps ahead) is set by a WALL-CLOCK DEADLINE rather than by a research choice. Setup: Turtlebot 3 Burger, pose (x,y,theta) from LiDAR + Nav2 AMCL, a small ReLU steering net (2 hidden layers of 64) trained on 100 expert trajectories at 20 Hz with NO obstacles in training, POLAR-Express (Taylor models degree 2 + Bernstein order 2 + symbolic remainders) run every 0.2 s over a 10-step horizon against obstacle footprints treated as the unsafe set, and a geometric counterclockwise avoidance law as fallback under a Simplex-style switch. Positive: the loop runs, detours single and multiple obstacles, and returns control to the learned net after each detour. Numbers (Table 1, one task each): horizon 10/15/20/30 gives per-call runtime 0.18/0.26/0.35/0.53 s, task total 77.73/80.05/82.32/89.31 s, fallback time 20.97/22.37/25.19/28.99 s, fallback utilisation 26.97/27.94/30.6/32.46% - a LONGER horizon (more foresight, more accumulated over-approximation) makes the robot SLOWER and MORE conservative, which the authors attribute to earlier and more frequent premature switches. Parameter sweep: TM degree costs time, BP order barely does, only TM degree <= 3 fits the 0.2 s budget (bar chart, no cell text). Critical gaps: no tightness/width measurement anywhere; no collision is ever staged to test whether a switch was NECESSARY (the safety evidence is that none happened); the fallback is assumed safe and recoverable (the authors name the unrecoverable-state risk themselves); the tool is only asked about obstacles perception already located; no competing tool, no repeated course. Reusable measure: the fallback-utilisation column is the folder's closest thing to a MEASURED PRICE OF LOOSENESS - the share of the task spent because the enclosure was unsure - reported as a property of the horizon rather than of the bound. arxiv-1804.04368 | Regularisation of Neural Networks by Enforcing Lipschitz Continuity | University of Waikato (Gouk, Frank, Pfahringer, Cree) | 2018-09 | 2 - the first member of the thread about the Lipschitz constant as a TRAINING object rather than a verification one: the full-network constant is the product of per-layer operator norms (exact for l1/l∞, a power-iteration UNDERESTIMATE for l2), enforced by projecting each weight matrix back onto a single-hyperparameter cap after every gradient step, giving a guarantee on the product bound and not on the model's true steepness. Two pieces of real engineering worth stealing: convolution's true linear operator is a block matrix of circulant filter matrices, so the cheap "flatten the filter tensor and take its largest singular value" shortcut everyone used is NOT the spectral norm and differs greatly in construction; and the power method can be run with forward+transposed convolutions so the spectral norm costs about one single-sample forward/backward pass. Results are accuracy only - LCC+batchnorm 93.25% on VGG CIFAR-10 against a 90.45% batchnorm baseline, 70.19% against 56.14% on CIFAR-100, best average rank on 7 of 10 tabular sets but NOT significantly better than batchnorm alone, level with dropout on residual nets, and the competing spectral-decay method fails to converge on WRN/SVHN (9.09%). Honest failure printed: layers constrained under l2 finished ABOVE the chosen λ once norms were recomputed, because training used a single power iteration - the bound stopped being a bound. No tightness metric, no measured constant anywhere, no wall-clock table.
arxiv-2004.13135 | Local Lipschitz Bounds of Deep Neural Networks | ETH Zürich | 2023-02 | 2 — parameter-space (not input-space) Lipschitz bounds for DNNs and their gradients, closed form in depth/width/weight-norm, with matched lower-bound constructions proving global bounds cannot exist; the bracket is printed at both ends and its width never reported
arxiv-2603.13334 | Lipschitz-Based Robustness Certification Under Floating-Point Execution | University of Melbourne (Toby Murray) | 2026-11 | 2 - the first paper in the folder to charge the semantic gap between real arithmetic and the arithmetic a model actually runs in, and the counterexample is the reusable weapon: because biases do not enter the Lipschitz constant, adding a huge constant bias to the last hidden layer and cancelling it in the output layer changes nothing in real arithmetic yet inflates the output layer's rounding error by ~6 orders of magnitude, so a formally verified certifier issues false certificates on ordinary test images (9,549 of 10,000 MNIST certified, 24 refuted; 204 on Fashion MNIST, 370 on CIFAR-10, all lower bounds). Fix: keep the real-arithmetic constant, add a per-layer deviation recursion bounding how far float outputs stray from real ones over the whole ball, interleaved with per-layer overflow inequalities; pre-deployment a single float64 pass measures the deviation and tightens the radii. Cost is small on five of six models (MNIST certified rate 95.74% real -> 95.50% worst-case -> 95.65% measured) and the CIFAR-10 exception (46.12 -> 18.90 -> 32.95) is driven by the input-radius/epsilon ratio, not model scale - same architecture on EMNIST-ByClass costs 1.16 points. Norms come from float64 Gram iteration with its rounding error charged, so the estimator over-estimates by construction and is orders of magnitude faster than exact rationals (19.5 s vs tens of hours), matching to 3.5e-11. 11-26x faster than a generously-config'd per-neuron baseline at float32 while retaining 98.3%+ of its own real-arithmetic VRA where the baseline keeps 1.3-70.0%.
arxiv-2311.16833 | 1-Lipschitz Layers Compared: Memory, Speed, and Certifiable Robustness | ISTA + Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna (Prach, Brau, Buttazzo, Lampert) | 2023-11 | 2 - the field's own controlled bake-off of seven 1-Lipschitz convolutional parameterisations, and the design decision that makes it usable is fixing WALL-CLOCK training time rather than epochs, which is the only fair axis when per-epoch costs differ by orders of magnitude (2h/10h/24h on one A100, 1.5M-100M params, CIFAR-10/100/Tiny ImageNet, certified accuracy at 36/255 plus measured inference throughput and peak GPU memory). Analytic cost table splits every layer into an input-side and a parameter-side transform and predicts the measured asymmetry: at inference AOL/BCOP add nothing over a plain convolution (parameter transforms cached), CPL/SLL pay 2x, SOC ~3x, Cayley/LOT ride the FFT (Cayley ~2x faster than LOT); at training the Fourier and cubic-in-channels methods collapse - LOT's large model exceeds 80GB. Accuracy is far less decisive: SOC best (66.3% certified on CIFAR-10 M), CPL most stable, Cayley last on robustness, ~65-66% vs 61-62% at 24h. Two cheap post-hoc audits (batch-activation-variance non-increase, proven in an appendix; per-layer convolutional power iteration) catch a released implementation (ECO) that does not produce 1-Lipschitz layers at all, plus NaN fragility in CPL and near-zero-division bugs in SLL's code - guarantees prove theorems, implementations need auditing.

arxiv-2004.08675 | CWY Parametrization for Scalable Learning of Orthogonal and Stiefel Matrices | University of Cambridge / Google Brain Robotics / Columbia / Alan Turing Institute (Likhosherstov, Davis, Choromanski, Weller) | 2020-04-18 | 2 - the computational-efficiency member of the orthogonal-parameterisation head: rewrites a product of Householder reflections exactly as identity minus a rank-L correction with a small upper-triangular solve, so the same algebra becomes a few dense GPU-friendly products, and truncates the same construction to give a proved-surjective Stiefel parameterisation; but this is a speed claim rather than a coverage claim (the full-L regime is exactly the Householder product), it covers O(N) only up to determinant sign, and its own ablation shows unconstrained recurrence with an orthogonal initialisation recovers much of the constrained model's gain on video
arxiv-1805.10408 | The Singular Values of Convolutional Layers | Google Brain (Sedghi, Gupta, Long) | 2018-05-26 | 2 - the ancestor of the survey's Fourier-domain reading of convolutions: proves that under the wrapping assumption a multi-channel conv layer's linear map is unitarily equivalent to a family of n^2 small channel-by-channel matrices, one per frequency pair, so its whole singular multiset is the union of those small spectra and its operator norm is the max over them - computable from weights in two lines of NumPy with no data; also the source of the doubly block-circulant lemma the 1-D state-space and certificate members later assume, and an empirical read-out of pre-trained ResNet-v2 spectra (largest norms near the input, peak non-negligible count in the middle, low effective rank at the end); its own regularisation experiment is the head's clearest case of a narrow binding window (6.2% to 5.3% at clip 0.5, back to 6.7% at 0.1) against trained norms already sitting at 2.5-2.8

arxiv-2104.05942 | Recurrent Equilibrium Networks: Unconstrained Learning of Stable and Robust Dynamical Models | University of Sydney (Revay, Wang, Manchester) | 2021-04-13 | 2 - the trade-journal counterpart of the head's bounded-equilibrium member and the cleanest statement of the family's central move: stabilise the coordinates rather than the loss. A feedback loop of one linear layer against a bank of slope-restricted units, where the nonlinearity solves a fixed point instead of unrolling into depth; the whole matrix tuple is built from a free parameter matrix A by A^T A, a small skew perturbation, and an exponentiated diagonal, so pointwise positivity of the activation scale is free and no LMI has to be solved per gradient step. Two sets, contracting and gain-bounded, with the bounded one differing only by adding 1/gamma inner products to E, B1, C1, D11 and P - i.e. by a change of storage function. Proves containment of the earlier robust RNN, the bounded equilibrium net, arbitrarily deep feedforward nets (as a strictly lower-triangular activation coupling), Wiener and Hammerstein block models and finite-impulse-response filters, by exhibiting the parameter choices. Benchmarks are F16 ground vibration and noisy Wiener-Hammerstein at matched parameter counts against RNN and LSTM, judged on a performance-versus-observed-sensitivity curve with the certified gain drawn as a vertical line; REN dominates the trade-off, observed sensitivity about a tenth and a hundredth of the RNN's, and crucially the observed lower bound approaches the guaranteed one as the prescribed gain tightens - so the certificate is tightest exactly where it binds. Costs: the gain is a sequence gain over a horizon rather than a per-step Lipschitz bound, no output feed-through, a simple incremental sector instead of richer repeated-nonlinearity multipliers, and every certificate variable is trained and never read
arxiv-2005.02828 | CS-TSSOS: Correlative and term sparsity for large-scale polynomial optimization | CNRS-LAAS Toulouse (Wang, Magron, Lasserre, Mai) | 2020-05-06 | 2 - the algorithmic layer under the head's certificate papers: two-level variable-clique plus monomial-block hierarchy, proved monotone and convergent, and the paper that names the failure mode of composing two sound relaxations (the naive per-clique version silently loses convergence); report block profiles, not just bounds

arxiv-1911.12859 | Decomposed Structured Subsets for Semidefinite and Sum-of-Squares Optimization | Northeastern / Harvard / Oxford (Miller, Zheng, Sznaier, Papachristodoulou) | 2019-11 | 2 - the paper that closes the sparse-certificate line: relax after decomposing, choose the cone per clique, and the relaxed block is an inner approximation whose optimism is a property of the instance, not of the method. Chordal cliques from the aggregate sparsity graph of the LMI, then DD/SDD/block-factor-width cones attached per maximal clique, with a proven containment order and the earlier theorems recovered as special cases. Reports the two extremes it sits between: DD infeasible on the undecomposed sea-star LMI but feasible decomposed (11.71 -> 1.282 as the threshold rises against a true 1.224), B_8 at K_11 in 2.7% of the full-SDP time; block-arrow B_10 recovers the exact optimum at -1.23 where B_1 gives 19.4; change of basis closes B_5's gap in 20 iterations. Explicitly denies that recovering the exact optimum from a relaxed cone is general, which is the missing caveat in every relaxed-certificate table this head has read
arxiv-2103.12444 | Exploiting Sparsity in Complex Polynomial Optimization | LAAS-CNRS Toulouse (Wang, Magron) | 2021-03 | 1 - background: ports TSSOS term and correlative sparsity to the complex moment-HSOS hierarchy; proves sparse-order monotonicity, finite-step convergence under the maximal chordal extension, and that the block partition refines the sign-symmetry partition. Complex arm is 9x faster on random multi-ball problems at a bound about 20% below the real hierarchy, closed to under 1% by raising the sparse order (block size 6 to 38, time 0.95s to 13.3s); on AC-OPF it certifies 6 of the 17 instances Shor misses against 11 for the real arm, but solves the 2869-bus case the real arm cannot. No network object; the transferable rule is that a bound must be reported with its block profile and chordal-extension strategy, since the same method and solver move the bound by tens of percent on that choice alone
arxiv-2103.06624 | Beta-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation with Per-neuron Split Constraints for Complete and Incomplete Neural Network Verification | Columbia / UCLA / Northeastern / CMU (Wang, Zhang, Xu, Lin, Jana, Hsieh, Kolter) | 2021-03 | 3 - central: the split constraint of branch-and-bound recast as a per-neuron multiplier vector inside CROWN's backward bound propagation, so the certificate carries one nonnegative "worth" per split neuron and is optimised by 20 gradient steps on GPU instead of an LP. Closes the verified-to-attack gap on an adversarially trained MNIST network from 35 points (SDP) to 12 at 27 min/sample against 1,274 min (47x), and is 2-7x faster at similar timeout rates than the strongest GPU dual-space verifier on the complete CIFAR-10 benchmark (median 5.11/4.05/7.25 s against 2421/3490/2982 s for LP-based search); the ablation separates the propagator's gain from the intermediate-bound gain (1% -> 5% -> 10% verified accuracy for an LP under interval, CROWN and jointly optimised intermediate bounds)

arxiv-2210.08069 | Zonotope Domains for Lagrangian Neural Network Verification | UT Austin / University of Washington (Jordan, Hayase, Dimakis, Oh) | 2022-10-14 | 2 - replaces the axis-aligned box that every Lagrangian-decomposition dual verifier constrains its intermediate variables with by a zonotope, so each subproblem becomes an exact "ReLU program" over a zonotope (proved equivalent to two-layer verification and hence NP-hard), relaxed by projecting the zonotope onto blocks of 2 coordinates where it is solvable in O(m log m) by a slope-sorted vertex walk - which interpolates monotonically between the box and the exact set and keeps the bound sound at every granularity. arxiv-2002.10410 | Lagrangian Decomposition for Neural Network Verification | University of Oxford / DeepMind (Bunel, De Palma, Desmaison, Dvijotham, Kohli, Torr, Kumar) | 2020-02-24 | 3 - central: the ancestor the head's whole Lagrangian family descends from, and the paper that shows the dual itself is the reading. Split the convex-hull relaxation of the network into one constraint group per layer, duplicate the boundary variables so each layer owns its own copy, and put a nonnegative-worth multiplier on each disagreement - so the dual's unknowns are exactly one per-neuron vector per layer boundary, and the sign of that vector pushed through the next weight matrix decides which relaxation case (passing, blocking, ambiguous) each neuron sits in, i.e. a per-neuron case map is computed every iteration and never printed. Both inner minimisation and the Frank-Wolfe conditional gradient are closed form (three vertices per neuron), so the primal operations are a forward pass and a transposed multiply and a whole batch runs on one GPU; proves the dual dominates the earlier relaxation dual at matched multipliers for ReLU and reproduces the Wong-Kolter bound exactly under its own initialisation, which is the warm start. The intermediate bounds that condition everything still come from interval propagation and Wong-Kolter for cost reasons, tanh is explicitly out of scope, and no per-layer multiplier profile is reported.

arxiv-2611.25165 | Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders | Stony Brook University / Concordia University + Mila | 2026-11-21 | 2 — full text (arXiv HTML v2, ~146k chars; abstract, §§1-6, supplement metric definitions (MonoScore, binary purity, KNN/LP, delta-CE/KL), Tables 1-2 and referenced supplementary tables as cells; figures 1-19 captions only, not inspected). DualSAE: split the SAE's two jobs. A Sparse Branch (any standard SAE: TopK/BatchTopK/JumpReLU/Gated/Matryoshka/CB) produces the interpretable code and a sparse reconstruction; a deliberately UNINTERPRETABLE Residual Branch predicts what is left (projector + nonlinearity on x minus sparse reconstruction) so the L2 loss applies to the SUM, not the sparse branch alone. The sum creates an identity-map shortcut, so they add a decorrelation penalty ||D_x^T r_hat||^2 on the residual prediction projected onto that sample's ACTIVE decoder directions, with the gradient argument spelled out: at the identity solution the reconstruction gradient vanishes but the decorrelation gradient does not, so identity is not stationary. Two-stage training (warm up sparse branch, then joint with decorrelation). Three controls that make it a real ablation: parameter-matched widened SAEs (18 paired rows, DualSAE wins every one), a sequential frozen-SAE + trained-residual baseline (lifts R^2 by 15.4-24.8% with interpretability UNCHANGED, which is how they show joint training rather than capacity is doing the work; DualSAE adds 10.5-43.3% MonoScore on comparable R^2), and expansion-ratio/warm-up/decorrelation sweeps, all over 3 seeds. Results: ~29% relative reconstruction and ~34% monosemanticity gain averaged over configurations; ImageNet-1K +27.1% R^2, +1.8% KNN, +1.2% LP, +31.2% MonoScore, +113.8% class purity. Language (Pythia layer 12): all four metrics improve for every variant on OpenWebText and GitHub code; GHC BatchTopK delta-CE 2.41->1.76 and KL 2.41->0.77. Downstream: topic diversity up in 89/90 configs, intruder accuracy 74/90, hypotheses more significant 17/18, steering qualitative only. Mine, not theirs: the residual branch's "non-semantic" status is an ASSUMPTION about what it absorbs (evidence is t-SNE plus per-branch KNN), and MonoScore is computed in the SAME encoder space the SAE compresses, which they acknowledge can reward latents for being close in that geometry (their own fix is a label-only purity metric; absolute values are not comparable to the original MonoScore paper). Limits they name: frozen pretrained encoders only, one LM, no end-to-end or multimodal, three new hyperparameters. Goal: understanding, evaluation-of-methods. Unit: feature, layer. Form: dictionary, decomposition. Method: SAE, other. Eval: downstream-task, ablation, benchmark.

Attention sinks are a learned brake on over-mixing: the multi-head over-squashing bound factors inter-token sensitivity into a product of head-averaged attention weights along each attribution path, so concentrating mass on one low-norm first-token value cheapens every path's product and turns the block into an approximate no-op. For us: a path-product attribution bound usable as a pre-ablation surrogate, the rule that a low-norm write is a function and not an inactive unit, and the requirement that structural ablations be repaired with an equivalent no-op. Chain of bounds: LC two-way related to LOCAL RANK (expected approx rank of the layer's input-Jacobian, rank_eps = count of singular values above eps - the same thresholded rank the folder keeps quoting), LC lower-bounds TOTAL VARIATION scaled by the network's largest Lipschitz constant (the robustness link), and LC <= (Frobenius norm)^L up to width/depth constants, giving an informal Theta(log(1/lambda)) weight-decay bound. The empirics are small and the authors say so: 4x200 MLP on 1,000 MNIST images at 2x He init - deliberately the favourable setting - where the LC drop coincides with adversarial-accuracy gain and the local-rank drop matches the SECOND of two LC drops; LC-LR Pearson 0.852/0.957/0.985 at layers 2/3/4 over six random cross-covariances with SD bars; weight-decay sweep fits R2=0.697 between the log(1/lambda)-type bounding quantity and final LC. arxiv-2503.08502 | The Space Between: On Folding, Symmetries and Sampling | Lewandowski, Heinzl, Pisoni, Moser (Software Competence Center Hagenberg; JKU Linz) | 2025-03-11 | 2 - the tooling follow-up to the ReLU space-folding measure, and the folder's cheapest template for invariance-first reporting: folding is chi = 1 - r1/r2 along a straight input path, where r1 is the largest Hamming distance reached from the start pattern in binarised activation space and r2 the total Hamming distance travelled, so a straight input line that scores high travelled far without getting far from where it started - folding, in the strict sense. Proved invariances, which is the portable part: extra steps inside one region leave chi unchanged (so the score depends on WHICH regions a walk visits, not how often), chi = 0 iff distance-from-start never decreases, flatness is path-direction-invariant while chi is not (their own 3-bit example reverses to a different score), and additivity fails in both directions with explicit counterexamples yet only sub-additivity was ever seen in trained nets. Generalises past ReLU by reframing linear regions as equivalence classes of identical binarised patterns, so any monotone activation (GELU, Swish, SwiGLU) works - ARGUED, NOT TESTED. Parameter-free sampling: step forward, halve the step whenever the Hamming gap exceeds one bit, accept at one bit or at the step floor; cost O(M*C) with M a few hundred typically, and the floor is the delicate parameter because adjacent regions can differ by more than one bit, in which case the walk silently merges them. Proposes a lambda/(Phi+1)^2 loss term with a log-sum-exp surrogate for the max - EXPLICITLY UNTESTED, and would require stopping training every n epochs. Empirics are inherited from a companion TMLR paper cited with no arXiv id: depth-dependence, folding up when generalisation error is low and down when it rises, and near-invariance to width at fixed depth on 60- vs 600-neuron nets. No tables, no experiment described, no baseline, no seeds; the only statistic is a Mann-Whitney intra- vs inter-class comparison reported qualitatively. Relevance 2, not 3: the object is a scalar geometry summary used as a training signal, not a white-box predictor, and the paper's real gift to us is method - prove a statistic's invariances before claiming it is diagnostic. ICLR 2025 workshop (weights as a new data modality). Not in SEED_QUEUE (Priority block empty); carried from runs 725-726, gate-tested free in both folders before fetch and again before this append.
arxiv-2310.12977 | Training Dynamics of Deep Network Linear Regions | Humayun, Balestriero, Baraniuk (Rice University) | 2023-10-19 | 3 - the phenomenon paper underneath four later entries in this arc, and the folder's cheapest partition statistic: local complexity = count of neuron hyperplanes that cut a sampled P-dimensional hull around a probe point, summed over layers, computable by ONE forward pass over the hull's vertices with no labels, no loss, no task - and it tracks the loss curve anyway, in three phases (initial descent, ascent, final descent). What it buys: the migration observation in its rawest form - during the final descent boundaries leave the training and test samples and pile onto the decision boundary, shown by exact partition slices through three points - and a control the later papers kept, the uniformly-random probe curve, which follows the test curve rather than the train one, so the train-side ascent is a data-proximity effect and not a global density change. What it costs: no tables and no statistics anywhere, the shape of the curve is the evidence and the absolute value is never characterised against r or P, migration is demonstrated in pictures plus a handful of slice counts rather than measured as a boundary-distance distribution, and the same manipulation (depth) moves the ascent peak in OPPOSITE directions on MNIST MLPs and CIFAR10 CNNs while the three-phase shape survives both - so the trajectory generalises and the effect directions do not. Also here: batch norm removes the final descent while raising LC everywhere (cited BN result: boundaries are pushed as close to the data as the data's spread allows), weight decay removes it but also flattens the ascent, width 2000 lowers the peak that width 1000 raised (overparameterisation read as implicit regularisation), grokking = memorisation during ascent plus a second small ascent before generalisation. No predictive claim: LC is computed and plotted, never used to forecast behaviour. Not in SEED_QUEUE (Priority block empty); run 728's top carried candidate, gate-tested free in both folders before fetch.
arxiv-2502.09954 | On Space Folds of ReLU Neural Networks | Lewandowski, Eghbalzadeh, Heinzl, Pisoni, Moser (Software Competence Center Hagenberg; AI at Meta; JKU Linz) | 2025-02-14 | 2 - the measured half of the ReLU space-folding programme, finally in the folder: one forward pass over a straight interpolated line, binarise every hidden activation, and fold = 1 - (largest Hamming distance reached from the start pattern)/(total Hamming distance walked) - a walk that wanders and returns near where it began scores high, and the score is proved to lie in [0,1] for any path crossing more than one region, boundedness offered as the reason it can be a cross-model reference point. Rests on a proved equivalence between Euclidean convexity of a union of activation regions and Hamming convexity of its bit patterns, which holds only for whole-space hyperplanes = FIRST-layer neurons, hence the claim that folding is invisible in a one-hidden-layer net (their re-derivation of the XOR depth requirement). What it buys: the empirically confirmed depth dependence the companion sampling paper could only cite - median peak folding rising with depth at Pearson 0.987 on MNIST 60-neuron MLPs, folding ~0.7-0.8 on the CantorNet fractal against much lower on MNIST, larger 2x300 / 3x200 nets barely raising the peaks while the share of paths showing ANY folding jumps 0.35/0.44 -> 0.97/0.99 (folding becoming pervasive, not stronger), and a k-means grouping study showing 5 centroids per class reproduce ungrouped values, which makes the class-pair sweep cheap. What it costs, and this is the part to carry: the 0.987 was computed on the ONE seed out of five where every depth trained well (deeper nets highly init-sensitive; the authors say so in the same paragraph), there is no table, no baseline, no untrained or shuffled-label control, no second dataset, and no statistic beyond that single correlation; uniformly spaced walk points are admitted suboptimal and the fix is deferred; and the one-bit adjacency assumption that makes a walk a walk is exactly what fails in deeper layers, which the companion paper repairs by halving the step until the bit gap is one. Reach beyond MLPs asserted, not tested (residuals yes, normalisation unchanged, attention out of reach). Relevance 2, not 3: a bounded geometric property with no predictive claim and no per-neuron attribution, salvaged for us as the sentinel statistic for "did this path leave and come back" plus the random-point null that should accompany it. TMLR 2025. Not in SEED_QUEUE (Priority block empty); run 729's top carried candidate, resolved by arXiv API on the title (no id in any text the folder held), gate-tested free in both folders before fetch and again before this append.

Limitations/Outlook, App.A pipelines, App.B metrics incl. the vfd = freq*(2*acc-1) decomposition, App.C Tables 1-4, App.D the two negative-result analyses, App.E KL fork tokens), no figure inspected. Qwen harmful advice: LLM direct, 100% acc / 3.4% freq; SAE via simplification rhetoric, 96.5% / 17.2% and bundling anaphoric pronouns. Gemini tables: LLM 'organized tables' 96.5%/11.4%/abs 3.0 vs SAE 'pipe and hyphen characters' 95.7%/9.2%/abs 1.33; LLM alone surfaces the Qwen length collapse (68.1 vs 495.8 tokens).
