arxiv-2106.08365 | Test Sample Accuracy Scales with Training Sample Density in Neural Networks | Ji, Pascanu, Hjelm, Lakshminarayanan, Vedaldi (DeepMind; Oxford VGG; Mila) | 2021-06-15 (v7 2022-07-28, CoLLAs 2022 oral) | 3 - central, and the first entry in the folder that answers the prediction question with a geometric quantity: a per-sample PREDICTIVE BOUND on the error of the linear subfunction a test input induces, computed from a frozen model, selected on a validation split and scored on held-out samples against a binary behaviour (correct/incorrect, in/OOD). The construction is the portable part: take the textbook per-region Hoeffding bound on empirical training error, notice it is infinite for the deep-net case because most test samples land in regions holding zero training points, and REPAIR IT BY SMOOTHING ACROSS REGIONS with a Gaussian kernel in Hamming distance between activation patterns - the smoothed mass P(h_i) enters the bound as 1/P(h_i), so the score is literally (weighted neighbour error) + (reciprocal of local training density), and a low-density subfunction gets a wide bound rather than an undefined one. This reciprocal-density term is the explicit version of what the folder's failing-boundary and random-probe controls have been approximating by hand since run 723. What they found, stated honestly: the average AUROC deficit from the best method per setting is -0.007 across eight baselines - which makes it 'competitive with entropy' (0.988 vs 0.989 AUCEA on CIFAR10 VGG16), NOT dominant, and the abstract's 'up to 20% absolute' is the CIFAR100 effective-accuracy best case (70-73% -> 90-92%) beside a ~7-point CIFAR10 gain that the sentence does not separate. Two cells in the appendix lose outright (ResNet50 CIFAR100 in-distribution AUROC 0.827 vs entropy 0.859; cluster distance 0.754 vs 0.750 on one OOD cell). What it costs: the partition is last-layer-only (so subfunctions are piecewise linear, not linear), the full bit space is used instead of the feasible set (density assigned to unreachable patterns), smoothing bias is argued reducible rather than measured, and the authors say outright that the continuous-representation version they would want needs a DIFFERENT bound - so transfer to a continuous feature space is a new derivation, not a reuse. Bonus machinery: Appendix B turns the exponential sums into O(M) and O(N^2+M^3) using Hamming-shell completeness and a binomial lookup, the same shell counting the folding literature's walks need. Log(t) scale, 1,000 thresholds, 5 seeds. Not in SEED_QUEUE (Priority block empty); run 731's top carried candidate, gate-tested free in both folders before fetch - note the carried description called it 'Shattering a Neural Network' but the real title is the density-scaling title above, so the gate's title-substring search on 'shattering' had to be read against the actual abs page before the fetch was trusted.
arxiv-2509.05485 | Prior Distribution and Model Confidence | Kazanskii, Kasianov (independent; no affiliation on record; code at github.com/maksimkazanskii/prior_hallucinations) | 2025-09-05 (v2 2026-01-26) | 3 - central, and the direct answer to the gap the partition-bound entry (arxiv-2106.08365) names as its own future work: a per-sample reliability score built from CONTINUOUS representation density rather than a discrete activation partition. Construction, in full: embed all of ImageNet-1K once in a frozen embedding model (six of them: DINO-v1 S/16, B/16, B/8; DINO-v2 S/14, B/14; MobileNet-v2 1000-d) and store the vectors; for a query retrieve top-K by cosine distance; declare the prediction confident iff at least N of the top-K lie within distance L. Two parameters, tuned on an ImageNet-V2 tuning split by maximising a normalised area between the accuracy-vs-coverage curve and the classifier's own all-data accuracy over coverage 0.1-1.0, then frozen and applied to three LABEL-DISJOINT partitions of each held-out test set, so every number is mean +/- std over disjoint class subsets - the right default for any per-sample score we report. Six ImageNet-1K classifiers (ResNet-50/101, DeiT-T/B/S, ShuffleNet-V2) x six embedding spaces, plus a continuous OOD score (mean cosine similarity to the N nearest neighbours) compared against Energy, Mahalanobis and ODIN. RESULTS, at full honesty: normalised gain 0.308-0.487 on the internal test set, best pair DINO-v2 B/14 in every shell except one (ResNet-101 0.477, ResNet-50 0.487, DeiT-B 0.480, DeiT-T 0.442, ShuffleNet 0.417); on ObjectNet where base accuracy collapses from ~0.68 to ~0.30 the same gains fall to 0.19-0.24 (0.096 for ShuffleNet). THE MOST INFORMATIVE NUMBER IS NOT THE GAIN: for five of six classifiers the tuned neighbour count is N=1, i.e. the filter is 'is the single nearest training image close enough' - a nearest-neighbour rule wearing a density label - and only the best embedding prefers k=7-60. MobileNet-v2 loses on every classifier despite the widest embedding and the largest parameter count, and the controlled 768-d comparison (DINO-v1 B/16 vs DINO-v2 B/14) credits DINO-v2 with 0.04-0.07 while extra dimensions within a family buy 0.01-0.03, so pretraining corpus beats capacity. Combining embeddings greedily is WORSE than the single best model in every case. OOD arm: on the internal near-shift set every method is at chance - embedding density 0.5867 AUROC on DeiT-Tiny vs Energy 0.5858, Mahalanobis 0.5850, ODIN 0.5878, FPR95 ~0.90-0.93 - so representation geometry has nothing to say about near shift; on ObjectNet Energy/ODIN reach ~0.90 and embedding density 0.851 (FPR95 0.4426), competitive but behind. Cost ~39h CPU encoding and ~8GB for the base table. LIMITS the authors name: the comparison is deliberately NOT representation-controlled (baselines read the supervised classifier's own features/logits, the density score reads DINO-v2 alone - stated in a named subsection); internal-set chance levels are conceded rather than explained away; text is blocked by the absence of a natural discretisation and by per-token storage at corpus scale; the 'more sophisticated embedding gives a better curve' claim bundles dimensions, resolution and pretraining data and is not isolated. Mine, marked: (a) the trade this paper makes is the folder's cleanest statement of what a bound buys - it keeps the density and drops the bound, becoming cheap and model-agnostic at the cost of the reasoned per-sample error estimate arxiv-2106.08365 derived; (b) tuned-k must always be reported, because k=1 says the installed mechanism is nearest-neighbour identity, not local density; (c) the label-disjoint partition control is worth adopting wholesale; (d) its chance-level internal AUROC across all four methods is quotable evidence that near-shift confidence is a geometry problem no scoring function fixes; (e) the filter optimises coverage-conditional accuracy, an aggregate, and never predicts WHICH class is right - the thing a white-box model must do. Chosen as run 731's carried candidate #1 (continuous representation density reliability score gated before naming) after the Priority block was found empty; id gate-tested free in both folders before the fetch and again before this append.
arxiv-2605.21493 | Don't Collapse Your Features: Why CenterLoss Hurts OOD Detection and Multi-Scale Mahalanobis Wins | Rahul D Ray (BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus) | 2026-04-10 | 2 - useful, and it supplies the counterweight to run 732's k=1 finding from the other side of the trade: a reliability score whose DIAGNOSTIC content depends on a within/between spread RATIO, and which gets WORSE when that ratio is pushed up. Pipeline: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 (45k/5k/10k), two taps pooled and projected to 512-d (stage-2 128-d texture + stage-4 512-d semantic), L2-normalised onto the unit sphere, tied class-conditional covariance fitted once with 1e-5 I ridge, minimum Mahalanobis distance as the score. Then a 3-input MLP (64/32, sigmoid) on [log(1+min-Maha), max cosine to any class mean, softmax entropy] trained with BCE against soft targets 0.05/0.95 on ID validation images plus a 50/50 mix of 5,000 SVHN 'hard OOD' and 2,000 Gaussian-noise images - so the score is a LEARNED FUSION, not a single geometric statistic, and it is supervised on OOD examples the evaluation partly shares a distribution with. Central claim, and the paper's framing is the useful part: classification geometry and epistemic geometry are not aligned. Adding CenterLoss raises the intra/inter feature-spread ratio from 2.5 to 7.5 (the manipulation demonstrably happened) and DROPS average OOD AUROC from 0.9483 to 0.9366 on CIFAR-10 vs SVHN/CIFAR-100-50/Synthetic, while costing one point of ID accuracy (0.9311 vs 0.9340). Mechanism offered: tighter clusters shrink inter-class margins, so a tied covariance becomes dominated by a few principal components and the Mahalanobis score compresses precisely in the between-cluster region where OOD points should stand out. Other ablations: dropping the early tap costs 0.0096 average (0.9483 -> 0.9270) and most on SVHN (0.9163 -> 0.8988), which is the cleanest result in the paper and the one the appendix's likelihood-ratio argument predicts; dropping SVHN from the calibration mix costs 0.0011 overall but 0.0249 on SVHN itself. Baselines: KNN 0.8967, ODIN 0.8870, deep ensemble 0.8827, energy 0.8800, plain min-Mahalanobis on penultimate features 0.6790 - the gap between 0.6790 and 0.9483 is the L2-on-sphere + multi-scale + learned-fusion stack, not anyone's geometry. WHAT TO DISTRUST, measured by me from their own tables: (a) the headline (0.0117) is SMALLER than the configuration's own seed spread - the five-seed study is run on the LOSING variant (CenterLoss, mean 0.9337 +/- 0.0085, range 0.9209-0.9448) while the winning variant is trained on exactly ONE seed (42), so no seed-matched comparison of the headline exists and the authors say the winner is 'expected' to be stable; (b) the average gain is carried by the two hard sets, the noise set being already saturated at 0.9980 -> 1.0000; (c) the calibration head is fitted on half of SVHN's test set, so the shift reported with the biggest single-set gain is the one whose shape the head was tuned on, defended only by disjointness; (d) the appendix theorems are conditional (uniform-alternative Gaussian mixture, served target soft labels treated as a posterior) and Theorem 4 'degradation' is a sketch whose proof argues both that tight clusters make distances MORE sensitive and that they overlap ID distances. Relevance: the folder's per-sample-reliability line now has both ends of a U - run 732 (a k-NN density score, optimum k=1, i.e. proximity) and this paper (a covariance-aware score hurt by over-compaction) - so the recurring quantity is within-class spread over between-class separation, which no entry in the arc reports as a number except this one, for one hyperparameter, on one dataset. Read fully (v1 HTML, 97,119 chars / 1,479 lines: abstract, §1-§8, Tables 1-4 reconstructed, Algorithm 1 lines 1-43, Appendix A.1-A.3 with all four theorems, reference list); Figures 1-2 read from captions only. Gate-tested free in both folders before the fetch and again before this append; carried candidate #1 for run 733 (does density beat proximity at k>1).
arxiv-2511.11934 | A Systematic Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Detection Under Representation and Training Paradigm Shifts | Claros Olivares, Brockmeier (University of Delaware) | 2025-11-14 (v4 2026-11-16) | 3 - central: the FIRST entry in the folder where the within/between-collapse geometry is used as a set of measured covariates that PREDICT, without any OOD data and without knowing the shift, which detectors will be competitive - and its own controls show exactly where that prediction stops working. Full text (v4 HTML, 302k chars / 8,773 lines: abstract, sec.1-6 incl. the full Limitations, App.A-G, App.H coefficient heatmap meat, App.K/L/M the three failed transfers, App.B the eight NC metric definitions and Table 5(a-c) of their values, App.I the worked regret row). Design: 22 CSFs x (VGG-13 from scratch | fine-tuned ViT) x 3 paradigms x 4 sources (CIFAR-10/100, SuperCIFAR-100, TinyImageNet) x 6 OOD sets, 5 seeds per cell; shifts stratified near/mid/far by k-means over four CLIP-embedding distances (three encoders agree, Spearman >= 0.83); per-cell Friedman -> Conover(0.05) -> Bron-Kerbosch cliques so the output is the set of detectors statistically indistinguishable from the best, not a rank list. The geometry is the classic 8: equinormness/equiangularity/max-equiangularity of class means and of classifier weights, Tr(Sigma_W Sigma_B^+)/C (Papyan NC1, reported /C), and the self-duality gap - all on TRAINING data, from a checkpoint alone. RESULTS: family transition is real and architecture-dependent (CNNs: probabilistic ID -> margin-based near -> geometry-aware CTM/fDBD mid/far; fine-tuned ViTs: abrupt, reconstruction/residual in every OOD regime); Mantel r = 0.37-0.70 (p <= 0.002) in all four strata, survives an accuracy control in all four, survives a source-identity control in 3 of 4 (Deep Gamblers dies). VGG-13->ResNet-18 transfer cuts mean set-regret vs the strongest fixed CSF by 55%/75%/80% (near/mid/far), 65 of 66 comparisons significant, shortlists of 8.1-8.4 of 22 CSFs. WHAT TO CARRY: (1) the random-shortlist-of-matched-size control, which almost matches the predictor on 47 ImageNet models (1.25 vs 1.05 pooled AUGRC x1e3; significant under the rank test, NOT under the mean test) and beats it on ViTs - so the predictor's advantage there is recommending a SET, not reading the geometry; (2) the transfer boundary is mapped, not assumed - inside a CNN family it works, on ImageNet families only the ResNet-50 recipes, on ConvNeXt it loses to random, and on 40 self-supervised probes it FAILS at far shift (8.08 vs 0.85 for Maha++); (3) cliques instead of winners as the eval shape; (4) coefficient signs are readable (CTM -1.47 self-duality, fDBD +5.39) but two heads picked almost no regularisation (C~110-160) with coefficients 10-50x larger and the authors say read signs, not magnitudes. Mine, marked: the collapse ratio is measured here but is NOT what carries the prediction - self-duality and classifier-weight equiangularity are - and the strongest single metric is max-equiangularity of W in 3 of 4 strata, i.e. feature spread matters less than the ETF structure of the head; the ViT failure is explained in App.B.4 by pretraining residuals (OOD lands inside pretrained subspaces, which is why class-conditional PCA filtering is the only thing that helps ViTs). One run per ResNet-18 cell means no clique exists on the transfer pool, so every transfer number is regret against a single-run oracle. Code MIT, zenodo (github.com/cesar-claros/ood_systematic). Not in SEED_QUEUE (Priority block empty); run 733's carried candidate #1 (the spread-ratio instrument), resolved by search after the named 'Liu & Qin 2025' / 'Momeni AnaNC' line returned nothing under those names; gate-tested free in both folders before the fetch and again before this append.
arxiv-2611.07753 | Neural Collapse on Imbalanced Datasets and Open-Set Scenario | Qiufu Li, Huibing Xiao, Linlin Shen, Yongdong Huang (Shenzhen University; North Minzu University) | 2026-11-05 | 2 - useful, and it is the theory that the folder's open-set / zero-support-class question needed: a derivation of what the last-layer geometry becomes when a class has NO training samples, plus the loss normalisation that restores ordinary collapse under imbalance. Core move: replace the globally averaged loss (one mean over all samples) with a CLASS-WISE averaged loss (mean within each class, then mean over classes), which is algebraically exactly inverse-frequency reweighting, and show that at its minimum the unconstrained-feature model attains standard NC on balanced AND imbalanced data: features = class mean = their own classifier vector, and both the class-centre gram and the weight gram take the ETF off-diagonal -1/(K-1). CE vs BCE differ only in the bias - free for CE, the unique root of an explicit quadratic for BCE (eq. 11). Open-set extension (Theorem 2/3): K_1 classes with data, K-K_1 classes with ZERO samples but a real classifier vector; at the loss bound the known classes keep a tight frame while every never-trained vector points along minus the global feature mean, so they all COINCIDE with one another and are orthogonal to the trained weights - and NC on the known classes is recovered exactly as the global mean norm goes to zero. Contrastive losses (Softmax/Sigmoid, normalised by positive and negative pair counts) get the same frame result. EVIDENCE, and the sharpest numbers in the paper are the BCE biases: measured 4.663-4.669 on CIFAR10-LT across IF 1/10/50/100 vs the predicted 4.6698, and 6.328-6.332 vs 6.3437 on CIFAR100-LT, on both ResNet18 and ViT-Tiny - agreement a free parameter cannot fake. Similarities sit near predicted constants (negative weight-feature approx -0.109 vs -0.111 on CIFAR10, -0.0101 vs -0.0101 on CIFAR100) with sd at or below ~0.01. The globally averaged loss is the contrast at IF=100: its similarity matrices span ~0.4 in off-diagonal value and grade monotonically from about -0.3 in the head classes to about 0.1 in the tail, i.e. class frequency printed into the angles, against a band under 0.024 for the class-wise version. Open-set: empty-class vectors reach ~0.999-1.000 mutual similarity by epoch 50, BEFORE the known classes settle. Known-class frame is recovered only as ||mean|| falls - K_1=90 of 100 gives norm 0.0186 and every statistic at the ETF value, K_1=30 gives 0.1544 where features collapse (0.9985) but no longer align with their weights (0.9871) even though each frame stays internally equiangular. ONE PREDICTION THEY REPORT FAILING: the empty vector should be exactly antiparallel to the global mean, but as the mean norm goes to zero the measured angle wanders (-0.6181 BCE at epoch 600; -0.2504 -> -0.0492 -> -0.0442 across CE stages), which they attribute to the direction of a near-zero vector being numerically arbitrary - a clean example of a theorem whose residual is a conditioning problem rather than a refutation. LIMITS (none named as such; read off the paper): unconstrained-feature model at the exact minimum, so the guarantee is asymptotic and several open-set rows are only approximate; every experiment on 10- and 100-class CIFAR with two small architectures; NO accuracy, AUROC or detection number anywhere despite the 'open-set' framing, and no baseline on any task metric - the globally averaged loss appears only as one violin figure; no seeds described for the reported sd; the Sigmoid contrastive version needs an extra weight on the negative terms because its inverse-pair normalisation shrinks inter-class separation as K grows. Mine, marked: (a) the loss normalisation is part of the geometry, not an implementation detail - per-class averaging IS inverse-frequency weighting, so two checkpoints with identical collapse metrics can owe them to different losses and any prototype-quality claim should name its normalisation; (b) carrying the measured mean +/- sd beside the theoretical constant in the same column is the cheapest honest-table shape in the folder; (c) the open-set theorem is the warning worth keeping - an untrained classifier slot converges to a specific direction with the same confidence and the same tiny variance as a trained one, so a zero-support direction reads as maximally crisp, which is precisely the failure a prototype-based OOD score would inherit. Read fully (v1 HTML 281,680 chars / 6,189 lines: abstract, sec.1-5, Theorems 1-4 with eq. 6-23 in full, Tables 1-4 reconstructed from the doubled-maths cells, sec.4.1-4.3 reporting prose, Table S.1 training settings, sec.S.1.1; appendix proofs S.2-S.4 not read beyond their statements). arxiv-2504.12569 | Let the Void Be Void: Robust Open-Set Semi-Supervised Learning via Selective Non-Alignment | You Rim Choi, Subeom Park, Seojun Heo, Eunchung Noh, Hyung-Sin Kim (Seoul National University; Samsung Electronics) | 2025-04-17 (v4 2026-01-16, AAAI 2026) | 2 - useful, and it is the folder's cleanest demonstration that a known-vs-unknown separation statistic can be MANUFACTURED by the training objective rather than discovered in the representation. Full text (v4 HTML, 82,424 chars / 1,925 lines: abstract, sec.1-5, Eq.1-9, Tables 1-6 reconstructed from the column-major cells, App.A.1-A.7 including the four gradient derivations and both Rademacher bounds with Theorem 1 and 2, App.B prototype blending, App.C.1-C.2 embedding commentary, App.D.1-D.2, App.E.1 algorithm lines 1-N and E.2 training details; Figures 1-9 read from captions and prose, NOT inspected as images). Core move, and it is one algebraic line rather than a new score: an unlabelled item is pulled to its predicted prototype only if BOTH a K-way softmax and a K-head OVA detector clear a threshold (the dual gate), and otherwise the positive term of the cosine-softmax loss is multiplied by zero, leaving only the tangent-plane projection of the softmax-weighted average of all prototype directions - a purely rotational, non-attractive update that nudges the item away from whichever prototypes it leans toward without attaching it to any. Their framing is a universe of compact ID galaxies inside a diffuse OOD void, and the loss is designed to keep the void empty. RESULTS: overall AUC (unweighted mean over 6-9 OOD sets) best in every configuration, up to +7.1 and +3.1 on average, closed-set accuracy up to +2.7 pp with small drops on CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet (60.2 vs SSB's 64.3 Acc on TIN while AUC goes 77.1 vs 75.7). Baselines IOMatch, SSB, ProSub, SCOMatch, 3 seeds, mean +/- sd in Table 1 only. THE ABLATION THAT MATTERS: Table 3 splits seen from unseen, and it says the labelled-only alignment losses buy NOTHING unseen (77.7 with no SNA losses, 77.7 with IA+PA) while the unlabelled skip term takes unseen to 79.1 - and seen is slightly HIGHER without it (91.5 vs 91.2), so the operator pays specifically on classes it never saw. Second sharpest number: removing the detector half of the gate (threshold 0) costs CIFAR-10 14.4 AUC points (80.0 vs 94.4) while accuracy moves 0.7 - the filter, not the head, decides the detection metric. WHAT TO DISTRUST, measured from their own tables: (a) Ablation Tables 2-6 are point estimates with no variance, while Table 1 gives +/- for the same cell (CIFAR-100 80/20-25 AUC +/-3.2, ImageNet-30 ProSub +/-3.4, SCOMatch +/-4.2), so the 0.7-AUC gap to the pull-only variant in Table 2 and the 1.7 for projection nonlinearity in Table 5 are differences below the spread the paper itself reports elsewhere; (b) all mechanism evidence is t-SNE plus a norm histogram and a cosine histogram shown only as figures - there is no table of either; (c) 'overall AUC' averages sets unweighted and the per-set breakdown lives only in a bar chart, so the LSUN exception the paper names is invisible in every row; (d) the dual-gate thresholds (0.99 classifier, 0.5 detector) are chosen and reported on the same two configurations. Mine, marked: App.A is the keeper - it writes the norm accounting explicitly, since cross-entropy, consistency and OVA all push ||f|| up along whichever weight vector the point is closest to in proportion to the cosine, so norm growth is confidence-times-alignment and a tangential update on uncertain items caps it; the resulting clean norm gap between known and unknown is therefore an artefact of the objective, and any reliability probe reading norm or prototype distance should be read that way. Read fully (v4 HTML); abstract page fetched first (5 authors, SNU + Samsung, AAAI 2026, code at github.com/yourimchoi/skipalign). Priority block empty; run 735's carried candidate #2 (train with placeholder slots for absent classes and MEASURE that geometry) produced only Zhou et al. 2021's placeholder paper, which is outside this run's date window and pre-theory; this paper was taken instead because its ablation is exactly the measurement that candidate asked for - the geometry of the non-ID region measured against unseen-set detection, with the objective varied as the causal handle (run 735's candidate #1 shape). web_search returned a daily-cap error this run, so discovery ran through the arXiv API (id_list and title/abs queries) instead; gate-tested free in both folders (python3 /tmp/lit/gate.py: aether:0 core:0 idx_a:0 idx_c:0) before the fetch and again before this append.
arxiv-2502.10691 | Controlling Neural Collapse Enhances Out-of-Distribution Detection and Transfer Learning | Md Yousuf Harun, Jhair Gallardo, Christopher Kanan (Rochester Institute of Technology; University of Rochester) | 2025-02-15 (ICML 2025) | 3 - central, and it is the folder's closest thing to the causal test the last two runs kept naming: the collapse level of a layer is a TRAINING KNOB (a nearest-neighbour entropy penalty on the encoder pulls it down, a frozen two-layer simplex-ETF projector pushes it up) and a behavioural error is printed next to the resulting NC1 at every setting. Core move: split the network so the encoder is kept deliberately uncollapsed for transfer (linear probe trained ON the OOD set) and the projector is kept deliberately collapsed for detection (energy score, FPR95), then compare the two embeddings of the same weights - VGG17 NC1 0.393 / 2.175 gives detection error 65.10 / 87.62 and transfer error 66.36 / 41.85, so changing embedding costs 25.70 of detection and buys 24.51 of transfer; ResNet18 0.341 / 1.762 gives 69.70 / 86.17 detection and 63.08 / 47.72 transfer; ViT-Tiny 2.748 / 5.769 gives 83.16 / 90.89 and 63.53 / 52.63. Across VGG17 layers NC1 correlates +0.77 with detection and -0.60 with transfer. THE ONE SWEEP, and the only place the axis is actually moved at controlled strength: Table 14, ImageNet-10 VGG17 without projector, entropy coefficient 0 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.6 / 1.0 gives effective rank 2211.99 / 2964.39 / 3170.92 / 3761.33 / 4815.32, transfer error 77.78 / 68.87 / 67.94 / 65.15 / 64.96 and ID error 9.20 / 9.80 / 10.20 / 12.00 / 12.80 - most of the transfer gain in the first 0.1, a roughly linear ID cost, and transfer WORSE at 1.0 than at 0.6. Mechanism ablations all move the wrong-metadata-free way: entropy penalty alone takes NC1 1.31 -> 2.18 and transfer 44.56 -> 41.85 with detection 67.46 -> 65.10; frozen ETF projector beats a trainable one by 8.9 detection points but loses 2.47 on transfer while WINNING 2.48 on ID error; group norm beats batch norm by 10.11 transfer and 4.37 detection with NC1 2.175 vs 1.401; CE beats MSE by 6.74 detection and 17.71 transfer. WHAT TO DISTRUST, measured from their own tables: no seeds, no variance anywhere (the words standard deviation and seed do not appear in the body), Table 1 and Table 2 are one number per cell; the trade-off is a correlation across layers plus a single coefficient sweep on a TEN-class ID dataset with a different architecture from the main results; the entropy side optimises a nearest-neighbour estimate of a density the classifier is simultaneously sharpening; every OOD set is a semantic shift at fixed resolution, so the paper's own claim that batch statistics break under covariate shift is never tested on covariate shift; and Proposition 4.1 only proves collapse implies minus-infinite entropy, which licenses the SIGN of the penalty and nothing about how much collapse it removes. Mine, marked: (a) collapse helped detection in every configuration, helped ID accuracy in one pair and hurt transfer, and the coefficient sweep shows the marginal benefit going negative at the top of its range - so a sign claim from one comparison would have been wrong and the direction is per-task and per-pair; (b) the encoder-versus-projector contrast is the cheapest controlled geometry experiment in the folder (same weights, two embeddings, two errors) and it is reproducible from a single training run. Read fully (v3 HTML 148,765 chars / 5,848 lines: abstract, sec.1-8, sec.2.1-2.3, sec.3 problem definition and the three error metrics, sec.4.1 with Proposition 4.1 and the KL/NN estimator derivation, sec.4.2 the ETF projector, sec.5 setup, sec.6.1-6.6 with Tables 1-9 reconstructed from the column-major cells, sec.7 Discussion, Appendix A-E, G Table 13-14 with the per-dataset cells, H.1 Table 15; Figures 1-9 read from captions and prose, NOT inspected as images; reference list not read beyond works cited in sec.1-2). arxiv-2512.07400 | Heads collapse, features stay: Why Replay needs big buffers | Giulia Lanzillotta, Damiano Meier, Thomas Hofmann (ETH Zurich, affiliation inferred) | 2025-12-08 (v2 2026-03-19) | 2 - useful, and it is the folder's cleanest case of the SAME knob moving the feature statistic and the head statistic at different rates: buffer size is swept over ten settings and the probe-recovered accuracy saturates almost at once while the network's own accuracy on old tasks recovers only near full replay. Full text (v2 HTML, 137,213 chars / 2,403 lines: abstract, sec.1-6 including Limitations and Broader Implications, sec.1.1 notation, sec.2 with the three empirical trends, sec.3.1-3.2 with the multi-head subsection, sec.4.1-4.3 with Hypotheses 1-2, Definition 1, Theorems 1-3, Corollaries 1-2 and the under-determined-classifier argument, sec.5; Appendix A.1 with Tables 1-3, A.2 figure details, A.3.1-A.3.3 with Table 4 and the norm-matching ablation, A.4 captions; Appendices B-C headings only; Figures 1-24 read from captions and prose, NOT inspected as images). Core move: two forgetting measures for every past task - shallow (output accuracy) and deep (a logistic probe retrained on frozen features) - plotted against buffer size (0/1/2/3/4/5/6/8/10/100 percent of each task dataset, three seeds, ResNet18 from scratch, pretrained ResNet50 and ViT-B, Cifar100 / Tiny-ImageNet / CUB200, ten tasks each, TIL/CIL/DIL). Small buffers pin the geometry, output accuracy does not recover until near-full replay, and the gap is far smaller in TIL. Theory: an input is OOD w.r.t. a checkpoint if its mean representation is orthogonal to the span of training class means (Definition 1, following NECO); once class means align with classifier rows the updates are confined to that active subspace, so an old class's mean component outside it is frozen or decays geometrically under weight decay (Theorem 1, mean scaled by (1-eta*lambda)^(t-t0)); replay is a mixture between the OOD and NC distributions with a mixing coefficient that grows with buffer size, giving a non-vanishing separability lower bound for any non-empty buffer (Theorem 3, Corollary 2) but no such guarantee for the head. Head-side mechanism: buffer covariance is rank-deficient and buffer means are norm-inflated, so the classifier's cost is invariant along directions the buffer does not span - a manifold of equally-low-loss heads misaligned with population mass. THE ABLATION THAT MATTERS, and it cuts against the theory's usefulness: norm-matching head initialisation (scale new heads to the existing heads' norm) does suppress the monotone growth of the centred-mean norm, and the authors state it has a negligible effect on final forgetting or accuracy - a mechanism confirmed and a behaviour unmoved. Second key number: in a d=10 bottleneck with 25 classes per task, NC1 and NC3 survive but pairwise-angle dispersion is about three times the standard setting's, and the gap persists, so the effect does not depend on the simplex being exact. Table 4 (Cifar100, ResNet, 5% replay): CIL 52.27+/-2.41 shallow vs 26.15+/-1.92 deep; DIL 46.38+/-1.88 vs 35.07+/-0.51; TIL 18.45+/-2.78 vs 14.89+/-1.77. WHAT TO DISTRUST, measured from the paper: (a) every number in the headline claim is read off a figure - there is no accuracy table for the main sweep; (b) the ETF-quality claim rests on figure dispersion, not a table; (c) the theory is asymptotic in the terminal phase and the authors say it ignores the transient where forgetting begins; (d) probe accuracy is only bounded through an SNR lower bound on a moment-based quantity, not the quantity the probe measures; (e) DIL's deep forgetting matching CIL is stated as a surprise and is one curve family in one figure; (f) no open-source code link for this paper (only the mammoth benchmark it was built on); affiliation not printed on the abstract or HTML, inferred from the author group. Mine, marked: the projection of an old class mean onto the active subspace is the cheapest readout-side reliability statistic in the folder - computable from weights plus a little data, and it produced the sharpest qualitative fact here, that after a task switch past-task means project onto the active subspace near zero and become indistinguishable from never-seen classes. Read fully (v2 HTML); abstract page fetched first (3 authors, v1 2025-12-08 / v2 2026-03-19, no venue, HTML experimental available). Priority block empty; carried candidate #1 (a collapse statistic swept with a behavioural metric and the turning point located) resolved to `2512.04034`, which is WITHDRAWN on arXiv with no PDF, so `2405.17816` (ICLR 2025) and this paper were compared and this one taken because it sweeps the knob with deep and shallow metrics in the same table-equivalent and states a signed prediction about which one moves first. web_search remains daily-capped, so discovery ran through the arXiv API (`all:"neural collapse" AND all:"out-of-distribution"` and friends); gate-tested free in both folders (python3 /tmp/lit/gate.py: aether:0 core:0 idx_a:0) before the fetch and again before this append.

Limits they name: onset convention drives lead, loop-then-EOS counts healthy, prompted or useful repetition untested, onset usually follows where healthy responses end so length is partly in the label, single reviewer per response, and a late judge onset on Apertus inflates warning coverage by up to 0.12. arxiv-2507.08218 | Simple Mechanistic Explanations for Out-Of-Context Reasoning | MIT / independent (Wang, Engels, Clive-Griffin, Rajamanoharan, Nanda) | 2025-07 | 3 (central: the folder's first model-diffing entry where a fine-tune is shown to be a direction, and the first where an UNCONDITIONAL constant vector implements a CONDITIONAL behaviour). Gemma 3 12B, 46 layers, four borrowed OOCR tasks (Risky/Safe, Risk Backdoor, anonymous-city geography, anonymous numerical functions), LoRA restricted to MLP blocks at rank 64 / dropout 0.05 / alpha 32, either all layers or one layer's down projection. Unit of analysis = one residual/MLP-output direction and its layer. Test set is out of distribution by construction, scored by top-1 accuracy and correct-minus-incorrect logit difference against base and all-layer LoRA. Single-layer LoRA matches or beats all-layer LoRA at its best layer (22 Risky/Safe, 2 for f(x)=3x+2, 15 for Tokyo) and all-layer LoRA shows negligible OOCR on Functions and Locations. Model diffing: read the adapter's output delta on 20 tokens of an in-distribution example plus 20 tokens of an unrelated Trafalgar passage, take the 780 pairwise absolute cosines, and they sit close to one for every task except Risk Backdoor, so the fine-tune is adding a direction. Extraction two ways (first principal component of the 20 deltas; mean of unitized deltas, scaled by the mean projection of the adapter output) reproduces LoRA behaviour in early layers with more variance and worse OOCR generalization. Directly trained vectors (norm-1 init, Adam8Bit, 20 warmup, no weight decay, injected at the MLP output before the pre-residual layernorm; final token only for Risky/Safe and the backdoor, token-conditional on codename tokens for Functions and Locations) also induce OOCR. Interpretability is a logit lens with hand-labelled top-10 tokens (non-English translated by Gemini 2.5 Pro): safe-behaviour vectors over layers 20-29 are caution-related across languages with the interpretable fraction falling in step with accuracy, while the Tokyo vector and the learned vectors are largely illegible. Learned vectors differ from the naive mean-difference construction and from EACH OTHER across five seeds (low pairwise cosine), so behaviour-preserving directions are a family. Backdoor: a vector added unconditionally at the final token produces conditional behaviour, validation accuracy about 1.0 on unseen in-distribution backdoor examples while OOD test accuracy is poor and below base, and patching the last-token query vectors from base into the steered model over a suffix of layers breaks the jailbreak, locating the condition in QK alignment rather than in the injection. Limits: one model, four tasks, no second family; the backdoor is an OOCR failure for both LoRA and vectors so it cannot say a task is unreachable; the paper declines to explain why SGD finds the simple solution and inherits steering-reliability caveats from Tan et al. rather than re-testing them; error bars over 5 seeds but the figures carrying them were read only through captions. Goal: understanding, safety/auditing. Unit: direction. Method: steering, weight-analysis, patching, model diffing. Eval: patching, downstream-task.

Task-level teeth unresolved: ARC-Easy shows the tax in NLL but no resolvable accuracy drop. arxiv-2606.10703 | From Observation to Intervention: A Causal Audit of Expert Importance in Mixture-of-Experts Models | Hasso Plattner Institute, University of Potsdam (Engmann, Adriano, Giese) | 2026-06 | 2 (useful: the folder's cleanest incident of the rung-1-to-rung-2 inferential failure, tested as a controlled experiment rather than argued). Three high-redundancy MoE LMs — OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 (16 layers, 64 experts, top-8), Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (24 layers, 60 routed plus one shared, top-4), DeepSeek-V2-Lite (27 layers, dense layer 0, 64 routed plus 2 shared, top-6) — activation rates 6.7% to 12.5%. Unit = one expert at one token position. Method: rank the token's active experts by a corpus-level observational metric (utilisation rate, activation norm, mean routing weight when active, activation std), zero out the top-ranked and the bottom-ranked, take the paired loss-change difference; a metric is valid only if that difference is reliably positive. n = 200 positions per metric-layer cell, 4 metrics x 5 layers x 3 models = 60 cells, WikiText-2 test split, paired t-test with Cohen's d and a 95% noncentral-t CI (bootstrapped, agreeing within 0.02), Wilcoxon as a distribution-free check with t-Wilcoxon disagreement counted as noise, Bonferroni at 0.05/20 = 0.0025. Control swaps the corpus average for the PER-TOKEN routing weight at the same position, identical n, corrected at 0.05/5 = 0.01. RESULTS: a three-model null — no cell survives the corrected dual test, all effect sizes below d = 0.23, signs inconsistent across layers; activation norm, benchmarked elsewhere as the strongest dropper criterion, never exceeds abs d of 0.157 (OLMoE activation std +0.141 at L11 flips to -0.020 at L15; DeepSeek utilisation +0.163 at L20 and +0.143 at L26 are uncorrected-only; Qwen activation std +0.222 at L23 crosses the corrected t-threshold but is rejected by Wilcoxon). The control recovers exactly one signal: OLMoE final MoE layer d = +0.231, CI [+0.09, +0.37], p = 0.0013, Spearman +0.199, growing monotonically with depth; Qwen within abs d of 0.124 and DeepSeek within 0.098, so the contrast is about where effects centre, not power. Progressive ablation (OLMoE, k = 1..7 experts removed, n = 500, layers L0 L1 L7 L8 L9 L15) explains the literature's pruning gains as a redundancy buffer: mean loss stays under 0.083 nats at k = 7 on layers 0 through 9, Layer 15 breaks at k = 2 (+0.155) and reaches +0.431 at k = 7 — but median at k = 7 is +0.018 with P95 +2.633 versus at most +0.709 elsewhere, so the cliff is a heavy upper tail on a minority of positions. Redistribution analysis dissociates two links: routing weight predicts residual-stream displacement at every layer in both OLMoE and Qwen (Qwen Spearman +0.558 to +0.744 over n = 34,016 activations), but displacement reaches logit-level compensation from Layer 6 in Qwen and only at Layer 15 in OLMoE; Qwen's displacement scales about 38x (0.011 to 0.440) without functional concentration, so displacement growth alone is not sufficient. LIMITS stated by the authors: CI half-widths near 0.14 at n = 200, so the claim is no reliable positive effect rather than exactly zero; one-expert ablation at one position against a one-shot global pruning pipeline; all three models high-redundancy (low-redundancy architectures such as Switch and Mixtral left open); the OLMoE signal is one model and one layer, an existence proof of a per-token predictor that needs the forward pass rather than a deployable metric. FOUR-TEST VERIFICATION SUITE before data collection: per-token CE against the HuggingFace reference, no stale state after clearing hooks, position diversity over 100 positions, and a position-specific ablation effect, all passed by all three models (DeepSeek repeated at each tested layer). TAKEAWAY for us: a copyable validity test (rank inside the active set, intervene top and bottom, require a reliably positive paired difference), the positive control at matched n that licenses reading a null as a centred effect, and the warning that a selection rule validated in a redundancy regime looks harmless because nearly every selection there is harmless. Unit: neuron, circuit. Form: graph, description. Method: ablation. Eval: ablation, faithfulness, evaluation-of-methods. Goal: evaluation-of-methods, understanding.

neuronpedia-circuits-research-landscape | The Circuits Research Landscape: Results and Perspectives | Anthropic / Google DeepMind / Goodfire AI / EleutherAI / Decode (Neuronpedia) | 2025-08 | 3 - full text (single rendered Neuronpedia page, 58.3k clean chars / 498 lines, one fetch; NO figure inspected - the MSE/L0 curves, the pruning grid and the kernel bar charts are images, so every number below is a printed sentence or a table cell). The coordinating report from the five labs that all built attribution-graph tooling (Anthropic, Decode, EleutherAI, Goodfire, Google DeepMind) on one method and its failure modes. Replacement model = cross-layer transcoder (CLT) writing to all later layers, versus per-layer (PLT) and skip variants; GPT-2 small and Llama 3.2 1B for the sweeps, Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B as replication substrates, 100M training tokens at roughly parameter-matched widths (2^17 transcoders, 2^15 CLTs, three times 2^15 incremental CLTs). Headline instrument is replacement score - the fraction of a PRUNED graph's influence arriving from input nodes rather than error nodes - read against mean per-token L0 on 260 curated prompts with an EOS token prepended to blunt GPT-2's first-token norm. Results: CLTs beat PLTs at matched parameters in the regimes of interest; JumpReLU best for CLTs but TopK/BatchTopK close and far easier to set; skip PLTs lower reconstruction error at fixed L0 yet score WORSE as replacement models (lower replacement score at a given MSE), read as error propagation through the bypass; incremental weight-tied CLTs match PLTs and fall short of CLTs. The most actionable number is a training rule: overshoot the desired post-pruning sparsity by roughly five to ten times at training time and let graph pruning remove the rest, because both already-sparse training and over-pruning are worse than this pairing. The KL-finetuning arm is the entry's cleanest negative: divergence between the fully patched replacement model and the original fell 0.33 to 0.20 while unexplained variance went 0.226 to 0.23 and replacement score FELL 0.723 to 0.705, so a surrogate can become a better mimic and a worse attribution at the same time. Two limitations outrank the wins: transcoders shatter geometric structure (a helix-and-trigonometry account of number is recovered as lookup-table features instead) and graphs are per-prompt execution traces, not algorithms - so many-prompt merging or geometry-preserving replacements are named future work, along with automated hypothesis generation and validation and downstream benchmarks that measure understanding. Engineering: torch.sparse CSR and the Triton embedding-bag kernels are within noise on a forward pass (0.87s vs 0.84s on 2^20 rows by 2^19 columns, 128 active per row); distributed TopK training hit 47.8 percent FLOPs utilisation, 53.8 with one published kernel family and 65.3 with a different activation. Relevance 3: it supplies the fidelity-with-attribution measure our white-box model needs (scored AFTER the description is simplified), the frontier-versus-point rule for any architecture claim, and the warning that any reconstruction-trained decomposition must pass a structure-preservation test separately from a loss number. Selection: Priority block empty in both files; SEED_QUEUE had this line as the last unread 'missing from queue' Goodfire entry, and a same-file note says it is NOT the manifold-steering post (that is core arxiv-2605.05115). Checked before taking: zero rows for its key or title in either INDEX, no file in aether/ or core/ under this slug, and two earlier queue picks were dropped because core/ already held them (the 'Why Larger Models Learn More' arXiv id 2605.29548 and 'Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability' 2501.16496).
goodfire-com-research-world-inside-neural-networks | The World Inside Neural Networks (Neural Geometry Series, position paper) | Goodfire (Geiger, Lubana, Fel, Merullo, Byun, Lewis, McGrath) | 2026-05-07 | 2 (useful) - full post, 19,141 clean chars / 189 lines, no figures inspected and no arXiv paper behind it; a position essay, so zero metrics anywhere. Thesis: concepts live on curved manifolds inside networks because training data inherits the structure of the world, so the manifold - not a direction - is the right unit for understanding and control. Two worked illustrations only: a mountain-car image-action world model whose car-position embeddings form a string (a curve fitted, then activations steered ALONG it, and the predicted car moves smoothly), where a straight path between endpoints instead passes through incoherent output and some paths land on a different valid activation and move the car elsewhere; and an unsupervised pipeline finding a slant-rhyme manifold in a language model (words ending -ore, ordered perfect to poor rhyme) whose SAE features do not name the rhyme, only local letter shapes (Hor-, Sor-, Dor-, import-, Cor-, morphology) - the shattering phenomenon, asserted not quantified. Builds an explicit three-level frame (representation, computation, behaviour) and says geometric structure is the data structure that computation consumes. Limits: illustrative anecdotes, no baselines, no held-out evaluation, no numbers of any kind, the steered-manifold result is shown on a toy world model not an LM, and the SAE-shattering claim leans on automated labels that are themselves the thing under dispute.

Tests whether the direction that DETECTS a behaviour is the one that CONTROLS it, geometrically. Positive control: output format (JSON vs markdown fences) is one vector doing both jobs - the lm_head { minus ``` direction detects and, at alpha 3.5 on layers 20-25, kills fencing on 100% of queries at 0.6% of activation norm, 0/100 random and 0/10 irrelevant-token controls, transplant 10/10. Interventions follow: DiM REDUCES refusals, hand-picked detection pushed at alpha 15 only drops fabrication ~70% to ~40% with 0 false refusals, SAE amplification to 50x and ablating 500 neurons both do nothing. Mechanism: at L25 the fake-vs-real gap on the detection axis is +49.8 (6.9x random) but the refusal gap there is -24.9, wrong sign, while the orthogonal residual (entity copy) is a median ~12x larger and larger still on real entities; removing the detection projection leaves Norlandia -> Nor essentially unchanged. Autopsy: MLP carries 5.66x the signal of attention (+42.3 vs +7.5) spread over L18-25; attention from L17 is dispensable and killing it lifts fake refusal 60% to 65%; a per-layer gate fails in all 9 conditions because the single-layer gap is ~0.01 while only the sum approaches 50. The double dissociation is the load-bearing claim: Llama refuses fakes 100% under identical near-orthogonal geometry, so its correct behaviour cannot flow through the measured detection direction. §8 kills the obvious shortcut - the cosine is a signature of the dissociation, NOT a steerability oracle, because measured consistently it sits near chance for steerable and unsteerable alike and what separates them is functional (the control direction's own detection AUC: ~1 for format, ~0.7 for refusal). Mine, marked: no figure inspected as an image, so pipeline/geometry plots are taken from captions and prose only; every number here is a printed table cell or an explicit sentence; the rotation sweep is the authors' own underpowered step and the stress test is where the real numbers are; and the paper's own limitation list (20-55 per condition, nothing above 10B, one behaviour deep-dived, entity-copy unexplained, lm_head linearity) is reproduced in the entry rather than compressed away.
